title: Joe Studwell on How Africa Works, and What It Tells Us About China
summary_zh: 本期节目中，主播Kaiser Kuo对话知名学者Joe Studwell，围绕其新作《How Africa Works》探讨非洲经济发展瓶颈、东亚发展模式的普适性及中国在非角色。Studwell指出，长期束缚非洲的根本原因并非腐败或部族冲突，而是历史上极低的人口密度与“低预算殖民主义”导致的市场缺失、城市化不足与教育匮乏。他以埃塞俄比亚为核心案例，剖析前总理Meles Zenawi如何效仿台湾与韩国推行小农农业与出口制造业政策实现减贫奇迹，同时检视其军工垄断与族裔联邦制的严重失误。此外，两人深入辨析了中国发展模式中普适性与独特性的边界，并指出当前中企赴非投资正从早期政策性基建贷款转向由商业银行和私营部门驱动的制造业，核心诉求在于逃离国内“内卷”以获取更高利润率。
key_takeaways_zh: 制约非洲早期发展的核心变量并非腐败或族群冲突，而是极低的人口密度导致缺乏市场规模、基础设施分摊能力与“低预算殖民主义”下的教育空白。
所谓的“东亚发展模式”（小农农业优先、出口导向型制造业、金融抑制与资本管制）本质上是全球快速工业化的通用最优解，在非洲成功案例中同样有效。
埃塞俄比亚在Meles Zenawi治下深入践行东亚型“发展型国家”路径并大幅减贫，但缺乏竞争的军工国企垄断与僵化的族裔联邦制最终诱发了惨烈内战。
中国发展模式的底层经济逻辑与日韩台高度一致，其真正独特之处在于“地方试点再全国推广”的政策机制以及1990年代通过拆分国企引入内部竞争的改革手腕。
中国对非经济参与已从早期政策性银行主导的基建与资源贷款，转向商业银行与私营企业驱动的制造业FDI，中企赴非的核心动机是寻求比国内更高的利润率。

highlights.title_zh: 东亚模式在非洲的普适性
highlights.summary_zh: Joe Studwell回顾受埃塞俄比亚和卢旺达政府之邀开启非洲研究的契机。他发现非洲取得经济成功的地区并无特殊秘方，而是同样依赖小农农业、挂钩出口纪律的制造业补贴以及服务于发展目标的金融管制。
highlights.quote_en: We call it an East Asian model, but it's really just the best global model that we have for rapid economic development.

highlights.title_zh: 低人口密度才是核心制约
highlights.summary_zh: Studwell驳斥了将非洲贫困归咎于腐败或部族主义的主流文献，指出1960年非洲人口密度不足每平方公里10人（同期东亚为70人）。极低的人口密度使非洲难以形成市场、分摊基础设施成本及产生城市集聚效应。
highlights.quote_en: How are you going to have markets with nine people per square kilometer? You're not going to have markets.

highlights.title_zh: 土地改革缺位与教育追赶
highlights.summary_zh: 由于历史上地广人稀且缺乏冷战反共压力，非洲独立后几乎未进行东亚式的土地重分配，白人定居者土地多落入本土权贵手中。不过，非洲将成人识字率从1960年的16%大幅提升，为如今人口红利释放奠定了人力资本基础。
highlights.quote_en: Fundamentally, land reform didn't take place in most African countries because there was a huge surfeit of land relative to people.

highlights.summary_zh: 埃塞俄比亚前总理Meles Zenawi在打游击期间便苦读台湾与韩国发展史，执政后在政府内部塑造了浓厚的学术研究风气。他坚持农业优先战略，派驻数万名农技推广员，使谷物产量翻三倍以上并大幅降低极端贫困率。
highlights.quote_en: That is the logic of the existence of the government is to develop the nation.

highlights.title_zh: 军工垄断与族裔联邦制之祸
highlights.summary_zh: 埃塞俄比亚偏离亚洲剧本的两大失误在于：组建缺乏市场竞争的军工联合体METEC包揽大型工程，以及推行划定族裔边界的联邦宪法。少数族裔提格雷精英幕后控权最终引发2020年惨烈内战，不过目前该国经济已重回10%的高增长。
highlights.quote_en: Really all it did, the federal system in Ethiopia, was to make people have stronger state identities, stronger ethnic identity.

highlights.title_zh: 中国在埃塞的基建与制造业转型
highlights.summary_zh: 随着“一带一路”倡议演进，中国对非资金支持已从政策性银行基建贷款转向商业银行银团贷款与私营制造业投资，去年中国对非制造业FDI达约120亿美元。在埃塞俄比亚，中国项目广泛雇佣本地劳工，且在非中国人展现出积极学习当地语言的文化适应力。
highlights.quote_en: Chinese firms put about $12 billion into manufacturing in Africa, and that's a big change from three-plus years ago when it was much more resources-focused.

highlights.title_zh: 中国发展模式究竟有何独特性
highlights.summary_zh: 在剥离东亚通用政策后，Studwell认为中国的独特性体现在政府治理能力上，如“先地方试点再全国推广”的机制，以及1990年代朱镕基不搞私有化而是将国企一分为四引入竞争的改革策略。
highlights.quote_en: He realized that, no, I don't have to privatize them. What I need is competition. If we get competition, we'll get better performance.

highlights.title_zh: 中企赴非的真实商业动机
highlights.summary_zh: 针对西方常见的地缘战略叙事，Studwell指出中企赴非投资并无宏大政治图谋，而是高度务实地顺应当地治理环境；当前中国制造商涌入非洲的核心动力，是逃离国内残酷竞争与低增长以博取更高的利润率。
highlights.quote_en: The main thing that I feel that Chinese investors indicate they want at the moment in Africa is better margins than they can get in China.

highlights.title_zh: 美国战略收缩与中国的角色
highlights.summary_zh: 过去十年美非贸易额下降约40%，加之2025年美国加征关税、反复无常地暂停AGOA待遇及裁撤USAID，严重打击了非洲出口服装业。尽管中国给予非洲最不发达国家零关税待遇，但中国自身进口制成品有限，未来需向当年世界银行援助中国那样提供更多发展支持。
highlights.quote_en: I don't know whether China will sort of seek to double down on its position in Africa given that the US is pulling back, but certainly, as things stand, China's the only game in town, really.

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Welcome to the Sinica Podcast, a weekly discussion of current affairs in China. In this program, we look at books, ideas, new research, intellectual currents, and cultural trends that can help us better understand what's happening in China's politics, foreign relations, economics, and society.
transcript.zh: 欢迎收听 Sinica Podcast，这是一档聚焦中国时事的每周讨论节目。在本节目中，我们探讨新书、观点、最新研究、思想动态以及文化趋势，帮助大家更深入地理解中国的政治、对外关系、经济与社会。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Join me each week for in-depth conversations that shed more light and bring less heat to how we think and talk about China. I'm Kaiser Kuo, coming to you this week from Mexico City.
transcript.zh: 欢迎每周与我一起展开深度对话，为我们思考和讨论中国的方式增添更多真知灼见，减少情绪化的喧嚣。我是 Kaiser Kuo，本周在墨西哥城为您播音。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Listeners, please support my work by becoming a paying subscriber at sinicapodcast.com. Yeah, I get how all these Substack subscriptions can really start to add up. I just did one this morning.
transcript.zh: 听众朋友们，欢迎访问 sinicapodcast.com 成为付费订阅用户来支持我的工作。我完全理解各类 Substack 订阅费用加在一起确实不少，我今天早上才刚订了一份。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: But I try and offer a lot. So, you get the Sinica Chinese Phrase of the Week from Andrew Methven, you get podcasts and roundups from the terrific folks at Trivium, the indispensable China-Global South Podcast, historian Jay Carter's This Week in China's History, the You Can Learn Chinese Podcast, and now in a new weekly feature which I hope you're enjoying, a Europe-China Perspective from Limun, which is a strategic advisory based here in China, run by René Ruschmeyer, a German fellow who's an excellent analyst and a very, very good writer.
transcript.zh: 但我力求提供丰富的内容。比如 Andrew Methven 主持的 Sinica 每周中文词汇，初纬咨询（Trivium）优秀团队带来的播客与综述，不可或缺的《中国与全球南方》播客，历史学者 Jay Carter 的《本周中国历史》，《你也能学中文》播客，以及我们新推出的每周专栏——由驻华战略咨询机构 Limun 带来的《中欧视角》，该机构由德国学者 René Ruschmeyer 主理，他是一位极具洞察力的分析师，也是一位文笔绝佳的作者，希望大家喜欢。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Please do subscribe so I can continue to bring you these conversations, these essays, and a lot more. My guest today is Joe Studwell.
transcript.zh: 欢迎大家订阅，这样我就能继续为大家带来这些深度对谈、专栏文章以及更多精彩内容。今天做客节目的嘉宾是 Joe Studwell。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: If you've spent any time at all thinking seriously about how East Asia developed, how East Asia got rich, you've almost certainly run into his 2013 book, How Asia Works, which did something I think very few books on development have really managed. It gave ordinary readers a usable paradigm on how it actually accomplished it: household agriculture first, export manufacturing second, a financial system bent to serve both of these.
transcript.zh: 如果你曾认真思考过东亚是如何实现发展并富裕起来的，那你几乎肯定读过他在2013年出版的著作《亚洲大趋势》（How Asia Works）。该书达成了一项极少有发展研究类著作能够做到的成就：它为普通读者提供了一套极具实用价值的分析范式，清晰拆解了东亚的发展路径——首先是家庭农业，其次是出口导向型制造业，再辅以全力服务这两者的金融体系。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And it did it in prose that you could actually enjoy. Before that, Joe wrote The China Dream, about the recurring foreign fantasy of the China market, and Asian Godfathers, about the tycoons of Southeast Asia and of Hong Kong.
transcript.zh: 而且他的文字流畅易读，极具阅读享受。在此之前，Joe 还撰写了剖析外资对中国市场反复幻想的《中国梦》（The China Dream），以及描绘东南亚和香港大亨的《亚洲教父》（Asian Godfathers）。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: He's been thinking about this part of the world for a very long time and thinking about it very well. So, it was a surprise, perhaps to him as much as anyone, that his new book is about Africa: How Africa Works: Success and Failure on the World's Last Developmental Frontier.
transcript.zh: 他长期深入关注并深入思考这一地区。因此，令人意外的是——或许对他自己也是如此——他的新书将目光投向了非洲：《非洲大趋势：世界最后的发展前沿之成败经验》（How Africa Works: Success and Failure on the World’s Last Developmental Frontier）。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It's out this year from Profile Books. And I want to say something about it before we start, because I don't often get to say this on the show.
transcript.zh: 该书今年由 Profile Books 出版。在节目正式开始前，我想就这本书说两句，因为在节目里我并不常有这样的由衷赞誉。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: As regular listeners will know, I was on a summer-long non-fiction fast. For months, I'd been reading nothing but novels, and I broke the fast, actually, with this book.
transcript.zh: 老听众都知道，我整个夏天都在对非虚构类作品进行“斋戒”。有好几个月，我除了小说什么都没读，而我正是用这本书打破了这场阅读“斋戒”。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I actually can't think of a better one to have broken it with. This is one of the most educational reading experiences I've had in years, you know, in part, of course, because I came to it knowing embarrassingly little.
transcript.zh: 我想不出还有哪本书更适合用来重新开启非虚构阅读了。这是我多年来最有收获的阅读体验之一，当然，部分原因也是因为我在阅读前对这一领域的了解少得令人惭愧。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: little about Africa, I came out of it not not with a pile of facts, but, you know, with a way of thinking about a continent of 55 countries, a framework I could actually carry around and and and test my ideas against, and that's that's rare.
transcript.zh: 读完之后，我收获的不仅是一堆事实，更是一种思考这个拥有55个国家的大陆的思维方式，一个我真正可以随时调用、用来检验自己想法的分析框架。这实属难得。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And I want to say why I think the writing works, because it's it's not an accident. I I think Joe writes with a kind of plain confidence. He's not afraid of of a number. The book is full of them, but every number is actually put to good use, to put to real work.
transcript.zh: 我想谈谈为什么我认为这本书写得如此成功，因为这绝非偶然。我认为Joe的笔触带着一种朴素的自信。他从不避讳列举数据，书中随处可见，但每一个数据都被用在了刀刃上，发挥了实实在在的作用。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And almost every African figure is set beside an Asian one at a, you know, comparable stage of development. So you're never asked to be, you know, just impressed or appalled in a vacuum. You learn, you know, that Ethiopia at its peak had 21 agricultural extension agents for every 10,000 farmers.
transcript.zh: 而且几乎每一个非洲的数据，都会与处于类似发展阶段的亚洲国家进行对比。因此，读者绝不会凭空感到惊叹或震惊。比如你会了解到，埃塞俄比亚在鼎盛时期，每万名农民配有21名农业推广员；

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And in the same breath, that China, which is, you know, celebrated for exactly this kind of thing, had just 16. He's equally unafraid of of, you know, rendering a judgment. He'll call constitution a profound mistake, you know, the federal system of Ethiopia, as we will get to.
transcript.zh: 与此同时，因在这方面表现优异而备受赞誉的中国，当时也才配有16名。他同样从不避讳给出鲜明的判断。他会直言不讳地指出某部宪法是个深刻的错误——比如我们稍后会聊到的埃塞俄比亚联邦制。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And, you know, a flagship industrial policy, he will call a vote-buying scheme, and he'll tell you why. Uh then there is the reporting. I mean, he did fieldwork in a dozen countries. Uh the book is just full of really nice reported scenes, lots of color.
transcript.zh: 对于某项旗舰产业政策，他会直接定性为“买选票的把戏”，并详细解释原因。此外还有扎实的现场调查。他在十几个国家进行了田野调查，书中充满了生动的报道现场和丰富的细节。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You know, farmers in Oromia and in Ethiopia sitting under an acacia tree telling him that their wheat yields have nearly doubled, and that their new problem is that they have nowhere to store the grain. A prime minister with a fertilizer status board in his office.
transcript.zh: 比如在埃塞俄比亚的奥罗米亚，农民们坐在金合欢树下告诉他，他们的小麦产量几乎翻了一番，现在的新烦恼是粮食多得没处存。还有一位总理，办公室里挂着化肥供应进展看板。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: 600 districts that are coded red, yellow, and green, actually getting on the phone, telephoning these officials in charge of the red ones, you know, where the fertilizer is is a problem. Uh the book is moving constantly between the view from, you know, 30,000 ft or whatever, to the view very much on the ground.
transcript.zh: 上面用红黄绿三色标注着600个行政区，他甚至会亲自打电话给亮红灯地区的负责人询问化肥短缺问题。这本书不断在宏观全局的万米高空视角与极具质感的微观田野视角之间切换。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And that kind of alteration is what makes a book about economic development actually harder to put down. It's not something I ever expected I would be saying. Now, um this is a China podcast, of course, and the book is not about China.
transcript.zh: 正是这种视角的交替切换，让一本谈经济发展的书令人手不释卷。我以前可从未想过自己会对这类书给出这样的评价。当然，我们这是一个关于中国的播客，而这本书并不是专门讲中国的。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: China appears in it, to be sure, but mostly as a yardstick, a a contractor, a lender, occasionally as kind of an object lesson. But there are two things I really hope to get at in this conversation that are very much about China.
transcript.zh: 书中确实提到了中国，但主要将其作为参照标尺、工程承包商或贷款方，偶尔也作为某种经验教训。不过在这场对话中，我非常希望能探讨两个与中国紧密相关的话题。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: The first is is what Joe's years of research on the ground have really revealed to him about China's involvement in African development, what he saw of it in a dozen countries, how it may have shifted his sense of the whole phenomenon of China in Africa, how the Chinese are regarded by the people he talked to, and where they have been more successful and less so, and why.
transcript.zh: 首先是Joe多年深入一线的研究所揭示的：中国在非洲发展中究竟扮演了怎样的角色？他在十几个国家的所见所闻，如何改变了他对“中国在非洲”这一现象的整体认知？受访当地人如何看待中国人？中国在哪些方面更为成功、哪些方面表现欠佳，原因又何在？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: The second thing I really hope to get at is something I have puzzled over for a long time. We talk about the East Asian developmental model as as if it were a thing, one thing, and
transcript.zh: 我真正想探讨的第二件事，则是困扰我很久的一个问题。我们平时谈论东亚发展模式，总把它当作一个铁板一块的单一整体，而……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: talk about China often as if it were either the ultimate expression of that model or something entirely its own. Ethiopia, which Joe says went all in on the Asian model, is about as good a kind of natural lab, a natural experiment, as we're ever going to get.
transcript.zh: 人们谈论中国时，往往将其视为这种模式的终极体现，或是某种完全自成一体的独特产物。而在 Joe 看来全力拥抱亚洲模式的埃塞俄比亚，则成了我们所能见到的最理想的自然试验田。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It's a large, poor, landlocked country that studied under Meles, studied Taiwan and South Korea really harder than any government in East Asia has ever studied anything, and then tried to actually, you know, put it into practice. So, what does Ethiopia's experience tell us about which features of that model actually are transferable?
transcript.zh: 这是一个面积广大、贫穷的内陆国家。在梅莱斯执政时期，埃塞俄比亚对中国台湾和韩国的研究，比东亚任何政府做过的任何研究都要刻苦，并试图将这些经验付诸实践。那么，埃塞俄比亚的经验向我们揭示了该模式的哪些特征真正具备可复制性？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And what, if anything, in the Chinese version of it is specifically Chinese? Is China, in other words, sui generis, or is it just the East Asian model at a scale nobody had ever seen before? That's actually a question that isn't settled in my own mind; I'm kind of agnostic on it and really hoping to hear what Joe has to say on the matter.
transcript.zh: 此外，在这种模式的中国版本中，究竟有哪些特质属于中国独有？换句话说，中国是自成一格的孤例，还是仅仅是将东亚模式推向了前所未有的超大尺度？这其实也是一直困扰着我、尚未定论的问题，我也非常期待听到 Joe 对此的见解。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: We're going to spend a lot of time on Ethiopia because that chapter is, well, I mean in my reading of it, kind of the heart of the book. And, you know, for a China watcher, it's the most fascinating thing in it. I also want to mention that I'm going to start another book on China and Ethiopia by Maria Repnikova, and I'm planning to have her on the show to talk about it, so consider this the first half of a two-part Ethiopian fixation. Joe Studwell, welcome at last to Sinica.
transcript.zh: 我们会在埃塞俄比亚上花不少时间，因为在我看来那一章堪称全书的核心。而且对于中国观察家来说，这也是最引人入胜的部分。另外我还想提一下，我马上要开读 Maria Repnikova 写的另一本关于中国与埃塞俄比亚的书，并计划邀请她做客节目，所以大家不妨把这期看作埃塞俄比亚专题的上半部。Joe Studwell，欢迎终于来到 Sinica！

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Thank you very much. It's lovely to be with you, Kaiser.
transcript.zh: 非常感谢，很高兴能与你交流，Kaiser。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You know, by wild coincidence, so I said I'm in Mexico City, I was on a panel with somebody who actually interviewed you about the book recently, Feyi Fawehinmi.
transcript.zh: 说来很巧，我现在在墨西哥城，刚好和一个最近就这本书采访过你的人同台做过讨论，他就是 Feyi Fawehinmi。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Ah, yes, yes, yes. Down in Cape Town. Feyi, yeah.
transcript.zh: 啊，对对对，是在开普敦。Feyi，没错。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And just last night at dinner, I was treated to a wonderfully rich graduate-level conversation with a Lagos-based development economist named Wale Lawal, who founded the magazine The Republic in Nigeria. It was a conversation in which I was able to participate thanks in large part to just having finished your excellent book. So thank you very much, Joe, for that.
transcript.zh: 而且昨晚晚餐时，我和一位常驻拉各斯的发展经济学家 Wale Lawal 进行了一场极具深度的研究生水准的交流，他在尼日利亚创办了《The Republic》杂志。多亏我刚读完了你这本杰作，才得以从容参与讨论。所以非常感谢你，Joe！

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Well, you're welcome.
transcript.zh: 哈哈，不客气。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So, let me start with the obvious question, which you actually anticipate in the first paragraph of your book itself, which is: what is somebody who is known for his work on Asia doing publishing this sweeping book on development in Africa? You tell the story of the Ethiopian and Rwandan governments inviting you in 2016 and your telling them it would be pointless because you knew nothing about Africa, and their insisting that it didn't matter, they wanted to talk about Asian policy and to benchmark themselves.
transcript.zh: 那么，我们先从那个显而易见的问题开始吧——你在书的第一段其实就预料到了——一个以研究亚洲闻名的学者，怎么会出版这样一部论述非洲发展的宏篇巨著？你书中提到埃塞俄比亚和卢旺达政府在2016年向你发出邀请，你当时告诉他们这毫无意义，因为你对非洲一无所知；但他们坚持说这无所谓，他们想探讨的是亚洲的政策并以此为参照系进行对标。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And then I guess you had this encounter with Bill Gates, and he asked you what you think about Africa. Anyway, walk us through how this whole thing became a book. I'm curious what you had to, among other things, what you had to unlearn along the way, what assumptions from 30 years of working on Asia turned out to be useless, or maybe even worse than useless, when you landed in Kigali or in Addis.
transcript.zh: 然后你似乎还与 Bill Gates 有过一次接触，他也询问你对非洲的看法。无论如何，请跟我们讲讲这一切是如何最终汇集成书的。我特别好奇的是，在这个过程中你必须抛弃哪些旧认知？在亚洲深耕30年所形成的主观假设，当你踏上基加利或亚的斯亚贝巴的土地时，有哪些被证明毫无用处，甚至适得其反？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Well, what you say...
transcript.zh: 嗯，正如你所说……

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Kaiser was what got it going. There were invites from the Ethiopian and the Rwandan governments, and Ethiopia in particular really impressed me. And then that was followed by this meeting with Gates, and he was saying, "Oh, what I really want to know is what you think about Africa, because that's where I'm spending my money."
transcript.zh: Kaiser，这一切就是这么开始的。当时埃塞俄比亚和卢旺达政府发来了邀请，尤其是埃塞俄比亚，给我留下了极其深刻的印象。随后我跟盖茨见了面，他说：“我真正想知道的是你对非洲的看法，因为我的钱都投在那儿。”

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And Gates was sort of connected with me via the How Asia Works book, because he'd flagged that as a book that he liked and he'd written about it, he'd blogged about it. So that's how I got involved.
transcript.zh: 盖茨之所以跟我有联系，是因为《亚洲大趋势》（How Asia Works）这本书，他曾把这本书列为自己喜欢的书，还撰文推介并在博客上讨论过。我就是这样介入这个课题的。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Really at the beginning, at the beginning I started out thinking that maybe there would be some special African sauce in policy terms as to what was necessary to development. Over the course of five years, when I wasn't doing this book full time, but I was doing it a lot of the time, I was disabused of that idea because where I found success in Africa, I found that it was connected to exactly the same policies that we associate with rapid economic growth in East Asia.
transcript.zh: 其实在一开始，我曾以为在政策层面，非洲可能需要某种独特的“秘方”才能实现发展。但在随后的五年里——虽然我不是全职写这本书，但大部分时间都在做相关研究——我摒弃了这种想法。因为我发现，非洲但凡取得成功的地方，其所依托的政策完全就是我们在东亚高速经济增长中看到的那套做法。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: So it was the focus on smallholder farming and agriculture more broadly. It was the focus on manufacturing and subsidy given to manufacturing, but conditioned on exports, which demonstrate that recipients of subsidies are producing globally competitive goods. And it was also to do with a certain amount of manipulation of the financial system in terms of having capital controls to trap savings at home, and also having banking systems—either private banking systems or public banking systems—could be directed to lend to the developmental targets that were set by the government.
transcript.zh: 具体来说，就是立足于小农经济乃至更宏观的农业；立足于制造业，向制造业提供补贴，但这种补贴必须以出口为硬性前提，以证明受补企业能生产出具有全球竞争力的商品；此外，还涉及一定程度的金融调控，即通过资本管制将储蓄留在国内，并引导银行体系——无论是私营银行还是国有银行——定向贷款给政府设定的发展目标。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: So those things actually, over the course of the research, turned out to be the same. And that, for better or for worse, came as something of a surprise to me. I thought Africa was going to be different. But subsequently, at the end of the book, I thought, well, why did I think it was going to be different, when in fact what we think of as the East Asian model isn't really the East Asian model at all?
transcript.zh: 在研究过程中，我发现这些内核其实如出一辙。不管好坏，这多少让我感到意外。我原本以为非洲会有所不同。但后来，到了全书收尾时，我反问自己：我当初凭什么认为非洲会有所不同呢？事实上，我们所谓的‘东亚模式’根本就不是东亚独有的。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Because it comes into Japan originally from Germany and other European countries, which in turn get much of their inspiration from the protectionist policies that were used by the United States originally, and which were a big influence on Germany. So, you know, we call it an East Asian model, but it's really just the best global model that we have for rapid economic development. So that was that bit of it.
transcript.zh: 因为这种模式最初是日本从德国等欧洲国家学来的，而欧洲国家的大部分灵感，又源自美国早期推行的贸易保护主义政策，这些政策对德国影响深远。所以，我们称之为‘东亚模式’，但它本质上不过是全人类实现经济快速腾飞最管用的一套全球通用模式。这算是一个方面。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: The bit that was completely different was the context in Africa, which is totally different to anything that we know in East Asia.
transcript.zh: 而截然不同的则是非洲的客观背景与条件，这与我们在东亚所熟知的一切完全不可同日而语。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Well, let's get into that, because, you know, the book's core argument is that Africa's relative poverty comes down to, for you, three historical factors, right? One is chronically low population density. A second is what you call low-budget colonial...
transcript.zh: 那我们就来深入探讨这一点。因为你这本书的核心论点认为，非洲相对贫困的根源可以归结为三个历史因素，对吧？第一是长期偏低的人口密度；第二是你所说的‘低成本殖民’……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And the initial conditions that those two things produced, your phrase is, "societies that were dispersed, fragmented, uneducated, and politically unorganized." And you say quite pointedly that it is this combination, and not the usual suspects of, you know, corruption, kleptocratic regimes, ethnic violence, that placed a ceiling over Africa's prospects.
transcript.zh: 这两者所导致的初始条件，用你的话来说就是“分散、割裂、未受过教育且在政治上缺乏组织的社会”。你还非常尖锐地指出，正是这种因素的叠加，而非通常认为的腐败、盗贼统治政权或种族冲突等常见诱因，构成了非洲发展前景的上限。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You know, it's a big claim, and I'm not familiar with all that much of the literature. I imagine it cuts against a great deal of the literature. So, Joe, how did you arrive at that sort of demographics as the master variable? I think many people don't think of Africa now, because, you know, it's so rapidly growing in population. We don't think of it that way.
transcript.zh: 这是一个非常重磅的论断。我对相关文献了解并不算深入，但我猜想这与绝大多数现有学术文献相左。Joe，你是如何认定人口学特征才是这一核心关键变量的？我想现在很多人不会这样看待非洲，毕竟它的人口正在如此飞速增长，大家通常不会从这个角度去思考。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: What kind of pushback have you had, or might you expect, from people who've spent, you know, careers on governance and institutions, focusing on those things, when you basically present them with this, you know, problem of low population density, some remarkable statistics that were really, really surprising to me?
transcript.zh: 面对那些毕生致力于研究治理结构和制度机制的学者，当你把低人口密度这一症结以及那些极其惊人的统计数据摆在他们面前时，你遇到了——或者预期会遇到——怎样的反弹？那些数据着实让我大吃一惊。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yeah. I mean, so far, to begin with the question about pushback, I haven't really had pushback, more had people in academia saying, "Yeah, it's odd how the demographic stuff was shoved to the side." I began the research process by reading, you know, big chunks of academic literature, reading through literature on governance, which in Africa tends to focus on patrimonial leadership.
transcript.zh: 是的。先回答关于学术反弹的问题，到目前为止我并没有真正遇到反弹，反而听到更多学界人士说：“确实，人口学方面的因素此前被边缘化显得很不可思议。”在研究初期，我阅读了大量的学术文献，梳理了关于治理的论著，而关于非洲治理的文献往往聚焦于恩庇侍从式（家父长制）的领导风格。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: So, the arguments are essentially that they appear to have judiciaries and parliaments and whatever, but the way that things actually get done is much more old-fashioned, you know, for want of a better word, tribal patrimonialism under chiefs. So that's a big literature. And the corruption and kleptocracy literature, saying that, you know, Africa is something different, is a big literature.
transcript.zh: 这些观点大意是指，表面上他们拥有司法系统和议会等制度框架，但实际的运作逻辑却非常古旧，姑且称之为酋长统治下的部族恩庇主义。这类文献体量庞大。另外关于腐败和盗贼统治、声称“非洲情况截然不同”的研究也占了很大篇幅。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And the ethnic fragmentation literature is a big literature, and that is actually the one that is cited as the most important in one of the most famous papers ever written about Africa, which is the one that came up with the idea of the "African dummy." And this means, in econometric terms, that putting Africa—Africa was the only thing that could explain a large chunk of African economic underperformance.
transcript.zh: 再有就是关于族群割裂的大量文献。在一篇关于非洲的传世名篇中，族群割裂甚至被视作最关键的解释变量。正是这篇论文提出了“非洲虚拟变量”（African dummy）的概念。在计量经济学语境中，这意味着唯有加入“非洲”这一属性，才能解释非洲在经济表现上的巨大落差。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: I mean, it's actually, you know, to me, to me at the end of of all of this, I felt that, not that the academics were sort of racist themselves, but I felt that that these lines of argument had a racist undertone. But what was not discussed, you know, and in the "African dummy" paper, the Easterly and Levine paper there, which was published in '97, it had a huge impact in terms of getting people to think that Africa was just cursed and different.
transcript.zh: 通读完这一切后，我的感受并不是这些学者本身带有种族偏见，而是这些论证逻辑底层带着一种隐性的种族主义色彩。但被忽视的是——比如在 Easterly 和 Levine 于1997年发表的那篇关于“非洲虚拟变量”的论文中，该文影响深远，直接导致许多人认定非洲就是背负魔咒、与众不同。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Right. Right, right.
transcript.zh: 对，确实如此。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: You know, this is the thing with econometrics, is they say, "Oh, we've tried everything..."
transcript.zh: 计量经济学的惯常套路往往是，他们宣称：“我们已经把所有变量都试遍了……”

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: we've checked every variable. Well, there's always a variable that they haven't checked. And if you go and look at that paper, then they haven't checked population density. And I got into that area in a couple of academic papers going back to the sort of 50s and the 60s where people said, look, at the end of the Second World War, Africa, whose surface area is big enough to contain China, and India, and Europe, and the United States, that's how big Africa is.
transcript.zh: “我们核查了每一个变量。”但总会有他们遗漏的变量。如果你去查阅那篇论文，就会发现他们漏掉了人口密度。我是在翻阅几篇可追溯至五六十年代的学术论文时接触到这个领域的，当时的学者指出：二战结束时，非洲的国土总面积足以容纳下中国、印度、欧洲以及美国，非洲的体量就是如此庞大。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: It had 220 million people in it, right? Which was like half of what China had at the time. But then you've got India, and Europe, and the U.S. The population density in 1960, when the comparable data for all the countries are available, was less than 10 people per square kilometer. So, you can just visualize what a square kilometer is and imagine having only 10 people—it was nearer nine people inside it. That's so few people.
transcript.zh: 可整个大陆当时只有2.2亿人口，对吧？差不多仅相当于当时中国人口的一半。更别说还要加上印度、欧洲和美国了。到了1960年，各国具备可比数据时，非洲的人口密度每平方公里不足10人。你可以脑补一下一平方公里有多大，再想象一下里面只住着10个人——确切地讲是接近9个人。人烟极其稀少。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And if you then compare, as I did when I was preparing the case I made in the book, if you compare that with Southeast Asia, which is relatively less populated part of East Asia, it was 50 people in 1960, and it then tripled over the next 60, 70 years. And in East Asia, so we're thinking of Japan and Korea and China, Taiwan, and those countries, it was 70 people already per square kilometer in 1960. So, then you get into the issue of why is this important? Why do you need people?
transcript.zh: 如果做个对比——就像我在构思这本书的论据时所做的那样——拿它和东南亚相比，东南亚在东亚算人口相对稀疏的地区，1960年每平方公里也有50人，并在随后的六七十年里翻了三倍。而在东亚，比如日本、韩国、中国大陆、台湾地区等地，1960年每平方公里就已经有70人。所以这就引出了一个核心问题：为什么这一点如此关键？为什么发展离不开人？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Help us understand what density actually does for development, mechanically. I mean, why is a thinly populated country so hard to develop, to grow? Why does your title for Chapter One call it a constraint rather than say an opportunity? You would think, with all that land available, isn't that sort of all that virgin soil untilled?
transcript.zh: 请帮我们从机制上理解一下，人口密度究竟是如何作用于发展的？我是说，为什么一个人烟稀少的国家会如此难以发展和增长？为什么你第一章的标题将其称为一种“制约”，而不是一种“机遇”？人们通常会以为，有那么多可用土地、大片未开垦的处女地，难道不是优势吗？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It's I suppose a little counterintuitive, but it was shocking to me, some of the stats in your book. Before, readers should know that 1900, you cited statistics that the largest cities in West and East Africa were only 20,000 people. I mean, that's a third the size of the little college town I lived in.
transcript.zh: 这确实有点反直觉。但你书里的一些统计数据确实震撼到了我。在展开之前，读者应该了解：你引用数据显示，1900年西非和东非最大的城市居然只有区区两万人。这只有我住过的那座大学城的三分之一大。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Well, at that point, Shanghai would have a quarter of a million already, and Singapore would have a lot more than that. So why does population density make a difference? It makes a huge difference because you've got to have markets, okay? So how are you going to have markets with nine people per square kilometer? You're not going to have markets.
transcript.zh: 要知道，在那个时期，上海的人口就已经有25万了，新加坡的人口更是远超于此。那么，为什么人口密度会产生决定性影响？因为发展必须依赖市场。如果每平方公里只有9个人，怎么可能形成市场？根本无从谈起。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Right. You need cities. Cities in order to have markets, but cities in order to have... Cities are massively more efficient as places for people to live than the countryside in terms of the costs of what people in modern societies want, in terms of the costs of...
transcript.zh: 没错。你需要城市。需要城市来孕育市场，但城市的作用不仅于此……从现代社会人们所需各项成本的角度来看，城市作为人类聚居地，其运行效率要远远高于乡村，无论是在基础设施成本方面……

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: infrastructure. Infrastructure, ultimately, is paid for on a per capita basis, and you need population density to be able to afford power stations, roads, railways, all of this stuff.
transcript.zh: 基础设施。基础设施归根结底是按人均成本来分摊支付的，你必须具备足够的人口密度，才能负担得起发电站、公路、铁路等所有这些设施。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And then you also need the things, what are called agglomeration economies by economists, that when you put people together, you get a better division of labor. You know, you'll get a narrower, more acute division of labor, which means that you have certain people who only do one thing, and certain people who only do another thing.
transcript.zh: 而且你还需要经济学上所说的集聚经济——当把人群聚集在一起时，就会产生更完善的劳动分工。劳动分工会更加细化和精准，这意味着特定的人专门做某一件事，另一些人专门做另一件事。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: That's what you get in cities. In the countryside, you get one guy who is supposed to do everything, but actually does everything badly. So cities, in that way, are also much more efficient at a fiscal level.
transcript.zh: 这就是城市所带来的优势。在农村，往往是同一个人不得不处理所有事情，结果样样都做不好。因此，从财政角度来看，城市也具有高得多的效率。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: I use in the book the example of the UK, because we have a good fiscal series by population density in the UK. There are nine regions in the UK, and only two of them produce a fiscal surplus, a tax surplus: London and the South East. And the South East region, basically, is a commuter belt for London.
transcript.zh: 我在书中以英国为例，因为英国拥有按人口密度划分的完善财政数据序列。英国有九个大区，其中只有两个能实现财政盈余、税收盈余：伦敦和东南英格兰。而东南英格兰大区基本上就是伦敦的通勤带。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Sure, sure.
transcript.zh: 确实如此。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: All of the other seven regions lose money on a per capita basis, and the least densely populated ones lose $7,000, $8,000, $9,000 per person per year. That's Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland.
transcript.zh: 其余七个大区按人均计算全部处于亏损状态，人口密度最低的地区每人每年要净亏损七千、八千甚至九千美元。这些地区就是威尔士、苏格兰和北爱尔兰。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: So you have that. The South East produces a surplus, and London produces a surplus. And if you look at that surplus, 70% of the UK's fiscal surplus—overall it's a deficit, because the loss-making regions lose more than the profitable regions, if you like, from a fiscal perspective—but 70% of the surplus in the UK comes just from London.
transcript.zh: 情况就是这样。东南英格兰产生盈余，伦敦也产生盈余。如果你分析这笔盈余，会发现英国全境70%的财政盈余——当然整体上是赤字的，因为如果从财政角度来看，亏损地区的赤字超过了盈利地区的顺差——但英国70%的净盈余仅仅来自伦敦一座城市。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And then, as I say, well, you can look at it a different way in terms of how things are affordable in London that are not only not affordable anywhere else in the UK, but they're not affordable in most places in Europe. So London recently built a new underground rail line called the Elizabeth line, which goes all the way from Heathrow in the west, right across London, and far off into the east, and it cost $30 billion to construct.
transcript.zh: 而且，你还可以从另一个角度来看：伦敦能够负担得起很多开销，这些项目不仅在英国其他任何地方都承担不起，在欧洲绝大多数地方也承担不起。比如伦敦最近新建了一条名为伊丽莎白线的地下铁路线，从西部的希思罗机场横穿整个伦敦，一直延伸到东部远郊，其建造成本高达300亿美元。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: London, nowhere else—it was reckoned that no other city in Europe could have afforded to pay for that line. But London could afford to pay for it, mainly with a local business levy in London, because 1.5 million people live within a 10-minute walk of an Elizabeth line tube station.
transcript.zh: 除伦敦外，据估计欧洲没有任何其他城市负担得起这条铁路。但伦敦凭借主要向本地企业征收的地方税就承担了下来，因为有150万人居住在距离伊丽莎白线地铁站步行10分钟的范围之内。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Right, right, right.
transcript.zh: 对，没错。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Let's go back a little bit, because we need to understand what the causes for that low density were. And above all, you cite disease. I mean, it's the mosquito, of course, the tsetse fly, everything from dengue and of course malaria to sleeping sickness. But there are other larger animals. Elephants—I was surprised how much...
transcript.zh: 我们稍微回溯一下，因为我们需要探究导致人口密度低下的根源究竟是什么。最主要的是，你提到了疾病。当然是指蚊子、采采蝇，引发从登革热、疟疾到昏睡病等各种疾病。但此外还有其他大型动物。大象——我非常惊讶它造成的影响竟然有……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: The space you devoted to the uh, that that sort of caught me off guard. I didn't realize that elephants had been the problem that that turned out to have been.
transcript.zh: 你在书中花了不少篇幅来写大象，这让我颇感意外。我之前完全没意识到，大象曾经是一个如此严重的问题。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yeah. I mean the start of the 19th century, the estimate is that there were 25 million African elephants in in Africa. And although they have a 22-month gestation, it's reckoned that there were periods when elephants were reproducing faster than human beings because of the disease burden that human beings were subject to.
transcript.zh: 是的。据估计，在19世纪初，非洲大陆上生活着大约2500万头非洲象。尽管大象的妊娠期长达22个月，但据推测，由于人类当时背负着沉重的疾病负担，在某些时期，大象的繁衍速度甚至超过了人类。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And the problem with elephants is that, you know, they're not like little cuddly Asian elephants. I mean, these are massive African elephants, and you cannot scare them away from anything, and they will eat anything that human beings grow.
transcript.zh: 大象的问题在于，它们可不像温顺可爱的亚洲象。这些庞大的非洲象根本无法被吓跑，而且只要是人类种植的作物，它们无所不吃。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: So, you know, if you go back to Tanzania in the 1920s in the colonial era and look at the colonial reports on the elephant problem, elephants were consuming every year between a quarter and a third of all crops that were grown, and there was nothing to be done.
transcript.zh: 如果你去查阅1920年代殖民时期的坦桑尼亚报告，看看当时关于“象患”的记录就会发现，大象每年会吃掉所有农作物的四分之一到三分之一，而人们对此束手无策。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And it took a very long time, and an awful lot of elephants had to be shot, and others were herded into these reserves, which they're now in, in northwestern Tanzania or in parts of Kenya. But it wasn't until the 1970s that wild elephants had had been controlled.
transcript.zh: 这耗费了极漫长的时间，大量的大象不得不被射杀，其余的则被驱赶进保护区，也就是如今坦桑尼亚西北部或肯尼亚部分地区的保护区。但直到1970年代，野生大象才真正被控制住。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And actually, even now, in places like northern Botswana, where they've been breeding rapidly and protected, they're now sort of reaching a kind of elephant population density where they are starting to cause trouble by heading back into human-settled areas.
transcript.zh: 事实上，即便在今天，像博茨瓦纳北部这样大象受到保护且迅速繁衍的地区，种群密度也已经达到了一定程度，以至于它们又开始侵入人类聚居区制造麻烦了。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Right, right. Well, let's move beyond the elephants, and then talk a little bit about one of the things that I underlined in your book: 'After independence, in almost every case, African governments failed to redistribute settler land to the growing ranks of subsistence farmers. Instead, they sold or passed it on to local elites, embedding the extreme land inequality introduced by the settler governments.'
transcript.zh: 对。那我们把话题从大象移开，来聊聊我在你书中划重点的一句话：“独立后，非洲各国政府几乎毫无例外地未能将定居殖民者的土地重新分配给日益壮大的自给自足农民阶层。相反，他们将土地出售或转交给了当地精英，从而固化了殖民政府带来的极端土地不平等格局。”

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Readers of How Asia Works are going to remember that land reform was your very first pillar. Japan, Korea, Taiwan, and for that matter, China itself, they all redistributed land after the war.
transcript.zh: 读过《亚洲大趋势》（How Asia Works）的读者一定记得，土地改革是你提出的发展第一大支柱。日本、韩国、中国台湾，乃至中国大陆本身，都在战后进行了土地再分配。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Why did essentially no African governments do this? And is that door now closed? Is it still possible? South Africa still has white farmers on more than 70% of its farmland 30 years after the end of apartheid, and you're skeptical even of the new Expropriation Act. So, is the door closed on land reform now, and why didn't it take place?
transcript.zh: 为什么几乎没有非洲国家这么做？这扇大门现在是否已经关闭了？还有可能实现吗？在种族隔离制度结束30年后，南非70%以上的农田仍掌握在白人农场主手中，而你甚至对新的《征收法案》也持怀疑态度。那么，土地改革的大门如今是否彻底关上了？当年它又为何未能推行？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Well, fundamentally, land reform didn't take place in most African countries because there was a huge surfeit of land relative to people.
transcript.zh: 从根本上说，大多数非洲国家没有推行土地改革，是因为相对于人口规模而言，土地资源极为过剩。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: So with much lower population density, you know, there was loads of land available, and the World Bank estimates are that still today, perhaps half of the world's unused cultivable land is in Africa. Now, there's a lot of variation. If you go around the Great Lakes, if you go to the Ethiopian Highlands, subdivision of land is creating a lot of pressure.
transcript.zh: 由于人口密度低得多，那里有大量可用的土地。据世界银行估计，直到今天，全球大约一半未开发的适耕土地仍在非洲。当然，不同地区差异很大。如果你去大湖区，或是埃塞俄比亚高地，土地的不断细分正在造成巨大的压力。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: But the situation in the independence era was nothing like East Asia, or, you know, nothing like it was across Japan, Korea, China, and down into Vietnam with higher population density. And in those places, of course, you get communist parties which are offering everybody a bit of land as a means of recruitment, as the People's Liberation Army did, or the Vietnamese Communist Party did.
transcript.zh: 但在非洲独立时期，其情况完全不像东亚那样，完全不像日本、韩国、中国乃至人口密度同样极高的越南。当然，在那些地方，共产党将‘分田分地’作为动员招募的手段，就像解放军或越南共产党所做的那样。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And then you get a response in East Asia from the US after the Second World War and, you know, on the advice of Wolf Ladejinsky and people like Ladejinsky, you know, we've got to do land reform in Japan and South Korea, because otherwise the communists are just going to, you know, we can't we can't hold the Cold War line.
transcript.zh: 随后，二战后美国在东亚做出了应对。根据沃夫·拉德津斯基（Wolf Ladejinsky）等人的建议，他们意识到必须在日本和韩国推进土地改革，否则共产党就会占领阵地，冷战防线将不攻自破。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You've got to get ahead of the communists, right?
transcript.zh: 必须赶在共产党人前面，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yeah, we've got to do this. So, Africa was really not like that, with a couple of odd exceptions. Yeah, so there was an exception in Zanzibar, which is now part of Tanzania, but was not part of Tanzania at the end of the Second World War.
transcript.zh: 对，必须这么做。所以非洲的情况完全不同，只有少数几个奇特的例外。比如桑给巴尔就是个例外，它现在是坦桑尼亚的一部分，但在二战结束时还不是。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And that had been run by the Omani emirs, the royal family of Oman, and basically it was a slave-trading island, and they owned all the land, and they had great big estates. And so, after independence, there was a move in Zanzibar to redistribute land, to move on from that kind of feudal Gulf approach to landholding. But that was unlike anywhere else.
transcript.zh: 那里曾由阿曼苏丹王室统治，基本上是一个奴隶贸易岛屿，他们拥有所有土地和庞大的庄园。因此在独立后，桑给巴尔采取行动重新分配土地，以摆脱那种类似海湾封建制度的土地占有模式。但这与其他任何地方都不同。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And then you have the case in Kenya where the so-called White Highlands, which had been reserved for white settlers, and were the best land in Kenya, there was an insurgency against the British colonial government, and that ended up with about a million acres being redistributed.
transcript.zh: 另外就是肯尼亚的例子，那里所谓的‘白色高地’曾专供白人定居者所有，也是肯尼亚最好的土地。当时爆发了反对英国殖民政府的起义，最终促成了大约100万英亩土地的重新分配。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: But in general, in Africa, it has not been the same. There hasn't been the need for redistribution, although in cases where there were white settler colonies, it would have been extremely helpful. But as I said in the book and as you were saying there, in places like Algeria, in Morocco, which are white settler colonies, in Mozambique, in Angola, there wasn't any serious redistribution of settler farmland.
transcript.zh: 但总的来说，非洲其他地方截然不同。那里普遍缺乏重新分配的紧迫需求，尽管在那些白人定居殖民地中，土改本会极具助益。但正如我在书中所言、以及你刚才所谈到的，在阿尔及利亚、摩洛哥这些白人定居殖民地，以及莫桑比克、安哥拉，根本没有对殖民者的农田进行过任何实质性的再分配。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: It tended just to be passed to cronies of the people in power, cronies of the Moroccan king or cronies of the Algerian government or whatever. So, agriculture has retained a very similar land distribution to what pertained in the colonial period. And then, as you mentioned, of course there's the particular case of South...
transcript.zh: 这些土地往往只是落入了掌权者的亲信手中——摩洛哥国王的亲信、阿尔及利亚政府的亲信等等。因此，那里的农业土地分配格局在很大程度上保留了殖民时期的样貌。此外，正如你提到的，当然还有南非的特殊情况……

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: South Africa, where it was put into the constitution, it was kind of the white price of giving up power in South Africa, that it was put into the constitution that there could not be forcible expropriation of land. And there has not yet been, and it's become more of a of a hot political problem in South Africa in the last sort of 10-15 years.
transcript.zh: 南非在宪法中明确规定了这一点，这算是白人交出权力的某种代价。宪法规定不得强行征收土地。到目前为止还没有发生强行征收，但在过去的10到15年里，这在南非已经变成了一个更加棘手的政治难题。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: But it's unusual in as much as the black population in South Africa was forced off the land so long ago, I mean we're often talking like 50, 100 plus years ago, that these people have lost all touch with farming as an occupation. And you know, farming is complex, even smallholder farming, and I don't think it's plausible that people who've got urban jobs, but a claim on rural land, are going to suddenly morph into smallholder farmers.
transcript.zh: 但它的不寻常之处在于，南非的黑人群体早在很久以前就被迫离开了土地——往往是50年、100多年以前——以至于他们完全脱离了农业生产。大家知道，耕作是项复杂的技术，即便是小农耕作也是如此。我不认为那些在城里有工作、仅拥有农村土地索求权的人，会突然转变成小农户。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: That's right, that doesn't happen.
transcript.zh: 确实如此，这不现实。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yeah, I mean, what is more needed in South Africa, I would say, is redistribution of white-owned land to provide small plots for homes and vegetable gardens for poor people. That would be a more kind of practical move.
transcript.zh: 是的，我认为南非现在更需要的，是对白人拥有的土地进行再分配，为穷人提供用于建房和种菜园的小块土地。这才是更加务实的做法。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So Joe, there are some more hopeful threads in the book, and one that I hadn't really appreciated at all was the education story. You describe a continent that began independence, you know, in the early '60s, with 16% adult literacy and just a few months of schooling per person on average.
transcript.zh: Joe，书中也有一些比较充满希望的线索，其中一个我之前完全没有意识到的是教育层面的故事。你描绘了整个非洲大陆在60年代初独立之初的景象：成年人识字率只有16%，人均受教育时间平均只有短短几个月。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And then you note that female literacy reached 48% by 1995, which is well ahead of the Indian subcontinent. You quote Nyerere, the British left Tanzania with two engineers and 12 doctors, and when he left office, literacy was down to just 9%.
transcript.zh: 随后你指出，到1995年，女性识字率达到了48%，这远远领先于印度次大陆。你引用了尼雷尔的话，英国人撤出坦桑尼亚时只留下了2名工程师和12名医生，而当他卸任时，不识字率降到了仅9%。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Now, how much of Africa's current moment do you attribute to that catch-up in human capital? And how much of the quality problem, you know, the 60% of sixth formers in some surveys that are not reaching minimum literacy, yeah, undercuts that gain?
transcript.zh: 那么，非洲目前的现状在多大程度上归功于人力资本的赶超？另外，质量问题——比如某些调查显示60%的中学生连最低识字水平都没达到——又在多大程度上削弱了这一成果？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yeah, I mean, I hear both things. There's a lot of concern about people who are formally in education in Africa that at present not achieving what they should achieve by the year, the grade that they get to.
transcript.zh: 是的，这两方面的情况我都了解。很多人担忧目前在非洲接受正规教育的人，在升到相应年级时并没有达到该有的学业水平。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: To be fair, that's America too.
transcript.zh: 平心而论，美国也是这样。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Well, but I think nonetheless, if you look back on what you referred to there as Africa as a continent that starts off in 1960 with 16% literacy. And I'm sure, Kaiser, you've heard all the stories about how well Taiwan did, or South Korea did.
transcript.zh: 好吧。但我认为尽管如此，如果回顾你刚才提到的情况，非洲大陆在1960年起步时识字率只有16%。Kaiser，我相信你一定听过很多关于中国台湾或韩国发展得多么出色的故事。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: You know, when you go and look at it, you're looking at like 45% literacy, okay? So, I mean the places that we hold up in East Asia as having been extraordinary in terms of the gains in the education system and out—
transcript.zh: 但你去查一下数据就会发现，它们起步时的识字率大约是45%，对吧？也就是说，那些被我们在东亚奉为典范、在教育体系发展和成效上极其非凡的地方——

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: comes since the end of the Second World War, they are, you know, not not even in the same league as what has had to be dealt with in Africa. And it goes back, again, to low population density, because that's the, what I call the, low-budget colonialism of Africa was determined by the fact that there was, these European colonists got there, and when they got there, they realized there was no viable tax base, because there were so few people.
transcript.zh: 自二战结束以来的情况，它们与非洲所面临的困境完全不可同日而语。这又得归结于人口密度偏低，因为正如我所说的非洲“低成本殖民主义”，正是由这样一个事实决定的：欧洲殖民者来到那里后发现，根本不存在可行的税基，因为那里的人口太稀少了。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Because cities, which always in, through history produced the most tax take in any society, the cities weren't developed, and the people were too sparse. So the colonists did not go to Africa in order to spend money, right? They went in order to, at a minimum, you know, extract a bit of money or extract resources. And it was, so they, they simply decided that we can't afford to run education systems.
transcript.zh: 从历史上看，任何社会的城市向来都是税收贡献最大的来源，但非洲的城市尚未发育，人口分布又过于分散。殖民者去非洲可不是为了花钱搞建设，对吧？他们去至少是为了攫取财富或榨取资源。因此，他们干脆断定自己负担不起建立教育系统的成本。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: So prior to the 1950s, there were almost no government schools in the whole of Africa. There were some more in North Africa, but in sub-Saharan Africa, almost no schools in the whole of sub-Saharan Africa, with the exception of small numbers of missionary schools. And that is how Africa found itself in a situation with only 16% literacy and 5% female literacy in 1960.
transcript.zh: 所以在20世纪50年代之前，整个非洲几乎没有公立学校。北非稍微多一些，但在撒哈拉以南非洲，除了少数教会学校外，几乎完全没有正规学校。这就是为什么到1960年，非洲的识字率仅有16%，女性识字率更是只有5%。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And I, and I say in the book, and I continue to believe it's the case, that Africa's achievement in getting most of its people through primary education and numerate and literate is a very considerable achievement that, that has been under-recognized. And it does, it does allow Africans now to take advantage of the growth possibilities that are coming with denser population.
transcript.zh: 我在书中提到，而且至今依然坚信：非洲让大多数人口完成初等教育并掌握基本读写算术能力的成就，是一项极其可观且未得到充分认可的突破。这确实让非洲人如今能够抓住人口密度提升所带来的增长机遇。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: One and a half billion people today, which is getting close to the 50 people per square kilometer that Southeast Asia started in 1960. And we'll have two and a half billion in 2050, and we'll have four billion on current projections at the end of the century. So really all the population growth in the whole world in this century is in Africa.
transcript.zh: 今天非洲拥有15亿人口，正在逼近东南亚在1960年起步时的每平方公里50人水平。到2050年，非洲人口将达25亿；按照目前的预测，到本世纪末将达40亿。也就是说，本世纪全球所有的人口增长实际上都集中在非洲。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And then at the end of the century, Africa will have four billion, Asia will have four billion, and the rest of the world will have only two billion, which will be psychologically very different place to be, right?
transcript.zh: 到本世纪末，非洲将有40亿人口，亚洲也将有40亿人口，而世界其他地区加起来只有20亿，届时的心理格局将会完全不同，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Indeed. Indeed.
transcript.zh: 确实如此，确实如此。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So, Joe, there's a sentence that you write early on. I want to put it to you because it almost feels like the rest of the book argues with it, right? You write, "Because of the different context, it is not useful to compare developmental performance in Africa with that in East Asia. Conditions in East Asia were far more immediately favorable to rapid economic growth after the Second World War than in Africa because, as we've talking about, of high population density, greater political..."
transcript.zh: Joe，你在书的开头写过一句话，我想拿出来和你讨论一下，因为感觉后面的内容几乎都在跟这句话较劲。你写道：“由于背景不同，将非洲的发展表现与东亚相比并无益处。二战后东亚的条件远比非洲更有利于快速经济增长，正如我们刚才所讨论的，东亚拥有高人口密度、更高的政治……”

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: ...maturity and much higher education levels. And yet, you know, you go on to compare Africa to East Asia on every page of the book. I mean, that's its method. So, I mean, how do you hold these things together? Because what's the right use of East Asia, this yardstick? What's the right use of it, and what's the wrong use of it?
transcript.zh: ……成熟度，以及高得多的受教育水平。然而，你在书中几乎每一页都在把非洲和东亚作对比。我的意思是，这就是全书的分析方法。那么，你是如何把这两者结合起来看的？究竟该如何正确运用东亚这把尺子？怎样算是合理借镜，怎样又属于生搬硬套？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: I think the right use of East Asia is that the policies that were developed and refined in East Asia in terms of smallholder farming that produces quite small gains per person, but spreads them very broadly across a population in which most people are farmers when a country is poor, that the use of that strategy, the use of export-oriented manufacturing to create the jobs that take these people off the land and into the modern economy, and the manipulation of financial systems to make sure that available capital resources support those objectives—these are all things that we can take from East Asia.
transcript.zh: 我认为借鉴东亚的正确方式在于，东亚所探索并完善的那些政策：比如在国家贫困阶段，大多数人口还是农民时，推行小农耕作模式，这种模式虽然人均收益微薄，却能极为广泛地惠及大众；又如利用出口导向型制造业创造就业岗位，将这些劳动力从土地中剥离并吸纳进现代经济体系；再如对金融系统进行政策干预，确保有限的资本资源全力支撑这些战略目标——这些经验都是我们完全可以从东亚身上汲取的。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Because those, although I said that those policies originate earlier on in Europe and the US, if you go back far enough, they—those policies were refined to a new level in East Asia. Still, you know, still—you can still see those policies in action, in real time, whether in China or in Vietnam.
transcript.zh: 因为尽管我前面提到，追本溯源的话，这些政策更早起源于欧洲和美国，但东亚确实将它们精炼到了一个全新的高度。至今，不论是在中国大陆还是在越南，你依然能够实时观察到这些政策在发挥作用。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: If we want to talk about places that are a bit closer in terms of context rather than policy to Africa, then within Asia, we're going to be thinking more about Southeast Asia, where we have countries that are more diverse in ethnic terms, you know, like Indonesia, like Myanmar, that have weaker government and don't have long histories of government operating, you know, in the national interest—I mean places like the Philippines. So there, we're going to see more parallels.
transcript.zh: 如果我们想在亚洲寻找与非洲发展语境（而非具体政策）更为相似的地区，那就更多要看东南亚了。在那里，各国的族群结构更加多元复杂，比如印度尼西亚、缅甸；政府治理效能相对薄弱，也没有长期以国家利益为导向的施政传统——比如菲律宾等地。因此在这些方面，两者之间能看到更多可比之处。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: But we've got to bear in mind at all times that Africa is lagging all of that development because, you know, as I say in the book, it hasn't been in the game until quite recently. Right. Just now, since the turn of the century, we can see, I think, the early indicators of a step-change.
transcript.zh: 但我们必须时刻牢记，非洲在所有这些发展维度上依然处于滞后阶段，因为正如我在书中所言，它直到最近才真正“入局”。确实。直到本世纪初，我认为我们才开始看到跨越式转变的早期端倪。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: The one that I cite most is the pickup in the growth rate of agricultural output, agricultural value added in Africa, which has gone up above 4% a year on average since 2000. And that's now ahead of China, it's ahead of Vietnam, it's ahead of Thailand. I mean, it should be, because the East Asian states and the Southeast Asian states are becoming ex-growth in agricultural terms.
transcript.zh: 我援引最多的一项指标，就是非洲农业产值及农业增加值增速的提升：自2000年以来，其年均增长率已超过4%。这一增速如今已经跑赢了中国、越南和泰国。当然，这也理所应当，因为东亚和东南亚国家在农业层面上已经基本告别了高速增长期。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: So there's just a limit ultimately to what you can get out of agriculture. It's not the same.
transcript.zh: 所以归根结底，农业所能带来的产出是有上限的。它和制造业不一样。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Right. You can only do intensive and no longer any more extensive, right?
transcript.zh: 没错。你只能搞集约化，再也没办法走粗放式扩张的路子了，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yeah, and it's not the same as manufacturing where you can just operate bigger and bigger and bigger and bigger production units and drive the cost down and down and down. But, yeah, I mean, I think that points of reference are useful. And then you hear them, I mean, like you hear them sometimes from Chinese people.
transcript.zh: 是的，它不像制造业，你可以不断扩大生产单元的规模，把成本一降再降。不过，我认为这些参照系确实很有用。而且你有时能从中国人嘴里听到类似的说法。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: I was looking around a textile factory in Ethiopia. There's a privately Chinese-owned investment zone there. And talking to the guy who was managing that, and he said, "Oh, you know, it's just like the early '90s here." Meaning, it's just like the early '90s in China. Yeah, yeah, yeah.
transcript.zh: 我当时在埃塞俄比亚参观一家纺织厂，那里有一个中国民营的投资园区。我和负责管理的负责人交谈，他说：“哎呀，这里就像我们90年代初一样。”意思是就像90年代初的中国。对，对。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: So, I mean, it was quite interesting as to hear his way of thinking through. And yeah, and he was saying, "Oh, you know, the productivity's not great, but they're keen to learn and they will get better. And the cost of labor is so low that you can afford quite a lot of inefficiency, right?"
transcript.zh: 所以听他剖析这里的逻辑非常有意思。他说：“哎，生产效率确实还不高，但工人们很肯学，慢慢会好起来的。而且人工成本极低，足以包容相当程度的效率低下，对吧？”

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah. Um, yeah, so let's plunge into Ethiopia. For readers, the book focuses on four African states, and you lay out your reasons very plainly for why you picked them. But they include Mauritius, which, you know, is almost not African. I mean, it's almost more of a South Asian than an African case.
transcript.zh: 没错。那么让我们深入聊聊埃塞俄比亚。需要向读者说明的是，这本书聚焦了四个非洲国家，你也很清楚地阐述了挑选它们的理由。其中包括毛里求斯，但这几乎算不上一个典型的非洲国家，感觉它更像南亚案例而非非洲案例。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You look, of course, at Botswana. But again, it doesn't have a lot of the Asian development model comparative propensity because, you know, it is so focused on its diamond wealth. And then the two that are more, and the two that I'll focus on, are Ethiopia, as I've said, and Rwanda, which is very explicitly gone after Singaporean-style sort of model.
transcript.zh: 当然你还分析了博茨瓦纳。但它同样没有太多亚洲发展模式的可比性，因为它的经济严重依赖钻石财富。而更具可比性、也是我接下来想重点探讨的两个国家，一个是刚才提到的埃塞俄比亚，另一个是卢旺达——它非常明确地在效仿新加坡模式。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So let's start with Ethiopia, and I want to start with Meles Zenawi, because the chapter is, in some ways, a portrait of his mind. For people who aren't familiar with him, he became president and then prime minister of Ethiopia after leading the EPRDF, the Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Democratic Front, to victory over the Derg, the junta with a comically villainous name that had ruled from 1974.
transcript.zh: 那我们先从埃塞俄比亚谈起，我想先聊聊梅莱斯·泽纳维（Meles Zenawi），因为这一章在某种程度上就是对他思想体系的剖析。对不熟悉他的听众来说，他曾领导埃塞俄比亚人民革命民主阵线（EPRDF），推翻了自1974年起统治该国、名字宛如反派漫画般的军政府“德格”（Derg），随后出任埃塞俄比亚总统，后改任总理。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Anyway, Meles, he was a guerrilla leader who carried around a copy of John Mellor's Agriculture on the Road to Industrialization through the last years of the civil war. He did an Open University MBA while actually already running the country, and he graduated top of his class.
transcript.zh: 梅莱斯曾是一名游击队领袖，在内战末期，他随身带着一本约翰·梅勒（John Mellor）的《工业化道路上的农业》（Agriculture on the Road to Industrialization）。在执掌国家大权期间，他攻读了英国开放大学的MBA，并且以全班第一名的成绩毕业。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: He wrote a master's thesis at Erasmus, "African Development: Dead Ends and New Beginnings," that was really a blueprint for Ethiopia, with five chapters dedicated to studying Taiwan and South Korea. He said it was primarily intended for our own local...
transcript.zh: 他在伊拉斯谟大学写过一篇硕士论文，题为《非洲发展：死胡同与新开端》（African Development: Dead Ends and New Beginnings）。这实际上就是埃塞俄比亚的发展蓝图，其中专门用了五章篇幅来研究台湾和韩国。他表示这主要是为了供他们本土……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: assumption to see if our policies could stand up to the rigors of some academic scrutiny. But this habit of his seems to have spread. In your book, you talk about these ministers and civil servants who were writing PhDs and books about the problems that they were working on.
transcript.zh: 假设，以此检验我们的政策是否经得起严苛的学术推敲。”但梅莱斯的这种习惯似乎流传开了。你在书中提到，那些部长和公务员甚至会针对自己负责处理的问题去撰写博士论文和专著。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I mean, there's probably no government in East Asia that ever studied other countries' experience quite so rigorously. You met the people that he left behind. What kind of a mind was Meles's, and what did that intellectual culture that he created there—what did that feel like from the inside?
transcript.zh: 甚至连东亚恐怕都没有哪个政府像他们那样严谨地钻研过他国经验。你也见过梅莱斯留下的班底。他究竟有着怎样的大脑？他在那里缔造的知识分子文化，身处其中是怎样一种感受？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yeah, I mean, he was an unusual freedom fighter because he was always thinking about what one would imagine that you probably should be thinking about if you're going to get involved in a war, which is, what are we going to do afterwards? And he was always obsessively interested in that.
transcript.zh: 是啊，他是一个非同寻常的自由战士，因为他始终在思考一个问题——如果你打算投身一场战争，这本该就是你首要考虑的——那就是：打赢之后我们要干什么？他对此几乎抱有一种执念。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: The weather in Ethiopia kind of helped him because there's a very wet rainy season—July, August, September—and the fighting in the war against the Derg would pretty much stop in that period. And so they would do, the EPRDF would do study sessions, and they had people bringing in books through Sudan and whatever.
transcript.zh: 埃塞俄比亚的气候某种程度上帮了他，因为每年七八九月是雨季，雨水极大，对抗德格政权的战事在这一时期基本都会停歇。于是埃革阵就会组织研讨学习会，还有人设法途经苏丹等地给他们捎带书籍。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And yeah, that vibe, that kind of intellectual vibe, is pretty deeply rooted. Even now, after the present premier, Abiy Ahmed, got rid of the EPRDF in 2019, and it's now been replaced by something called the Prosperity Party.
transcript.zh: 那种氛围，那种充满求知欲的底色扎根极深。即使到了现在，现任总理阿比·艾哈迈德在2019年取缔了埃革阵，并改组为所谓的“繁荣党”。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: But even then, I was very struck that after my book came out, and I had never met Abiy, but I got a nine-page letter signed by Abiy, which is basically a deconstruction of my book. And I thought, what other country, what other government is going to do that?
transcript.zh: 即便在如今，我也大为震撼：在我那本书出版后——我从未见过阿比——但我收到了一封由阿比亲笔签名的长达9页的信件，基本上是对我那本书的全面拆解剖析。我不禁想，还有哪个国家、哪届政府会这么做？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: I don't know, so that's the Ethiopian vibe. And it does really remind you of the kind of the vibe that you sometimes get from the Chinese government. I was not there soon enough, but I imagined that you got from the Taiwanese and the Korean governments, and that you get now from the Vietnamese government.
transcript.zh: 我不清楚，但这就是埃塞俄比亚的独特氛围。这确实会让人联想起有时在中国政府身上感受到的那种行事气场。我没能更早亲历当年的台湾或韩国，但我猜以前的台湾地区和韩国政府也是这样，现在的越南政府也是如此。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: It's just it is the developmental state thing. That is the logic of the existence of the government is to develop the nation.
transcript.zh: 这就是典型的“发展型国家”。政府存在的底层逻辑，就是为了发展这个国家。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So the first thing that the EPRDF does after taking Addis in 1991 was to publish a 34-page plan that put 85% of the population, the farmers, first. This is, the Joe Studwell method, right? Agricultural development-led industrialization.
transcript.zh: 埃革阵在1991年攻占亚的斯亚贝巴后，所做的第一件事就是发布了一份34页的规划，把占人口85%的农民放在首位。这就是所谓的“Joe Studwell发展法”，对吧？以农业发展为先导的工业化。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Very much of a focus on fertilizer. I was talking, you know, in my intro about the red, the yellow, and the green zones of—
transcript.zh: 其中极为侧重化肥推广。我在开场白中也提到了他们划分的红区、黄区和绿区——

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: ...fertilizer density, seeds, of course. Tens of thousands of extension agents everywhere, rural roads.
transcript.zh: ……化肥投入强度，当然还有种子。随处可见数以万计的农业推广员，还有农村公路。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: A PM who chaired the agriculture meetings himself, and handed out prizes himself at farmers' festivals. And the results, as you cite in the book, are quite impressive, staggering maybe, cereal output that roughly triples. Extreme poverty that goes from 69% to just 31% in a very, very short period.
transcript.zh: 一位亲自主持农业会议的总理，甚至在农民节日上亲自颁奖。正如你在书中所引用的，其成果相当可观，甚至是惊人的，粮食产量几乎翻了三倍。极度贫困率在非常短的时间内从69%降至仅31%。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: How much of that was, I mean, I imagine a lot of it must have been the sort of explicit Asian borrowing, Taiwan's Joint Commission on Rural Reconstruction reborn now as the Agricultural Transformation Agency in Ethiopia? How much was Ethiopia kind of working stuff out for itself? And why didn't it spread?
transcript.zh: 其中有多少是，我是说，我想很大一部分肯定是对亚洲模式的明确借鉴，比如台湾的农村复兴联合委员会如今在埃塞俄比亚摇身一变成为农业转型署？又有多少是埃塞俄比亚自己摸索出来的？以及，为什么这种模式没有向外传播？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Why didn't, Meles has this idea about hegemony, kind of in the Gramscian sense. Why didn't developmental hegemony kind of spread beyond Ethiopia in the 90s?
transcript.zh: 为什么没有，梅莱斯有一种关于霸权的想法，有点像葛兰西意义上的霸权。为什么这种发展型霸权在90年代没能扩散到埃塞俄比亚之外呢？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yeah, it's a good question. So in a sense we can say that it spread a bit to Rwanda because Meles and Kagame, I don't know how close they were, but they certainly did a lot together. They sort of did a lot of events together, they met a lot together, and I think they both regarded each other as developmentally serious.
transcript.zh: 是的，问得好。从某种意义上说，我们可以认为它向卢旺达传播了一点，因为梅莱斯和卡加梅，我不知道他们私交有多深，但他们确实经常一起行动。他们一起出席了很多活动，频繁会晤，我认为他们都把对方视作在国家发展上动真格的人。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, I mean, they were both always present at the World Economic Forum meetings in Davos. I've met Kagame there and I know Meles used to be a regular.
transcript.zh: 是啊，他们以前总是出席达沃斯世界经济论坛年会。我在那里见过卡加梅，而且我知道梅莱斯以前也是常客。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yeah. But why it didn't spread to other countries, I mean, I think that, you know, they didn't have, they just didn't have the right leadership at the time in the 90s. And it's only sort of now that you feel that governments are a bit more, a bit more receptive to ideas about significant policy change.
transcript.zh: 对。但为什么它没有向其他国家传播，我认为，在90年代那个时候，其他国家根本没有合适的领导层。直到现在，你才隐约感觉到各国政府对重大政策变革的想法稍微更加开放包容了一些。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And you get, I mean, in Benin, for instance, we've had Talon who's already served two terms, but now his deputy is serving, and they have this kind of developmental state vibe as well. So there seems to be a sort of a very slow trickle of it.
transcript.zh: 比如在贝宁，塔隆已经连任两届，现在由他的副手执政，他们身上也带有这种发展型国家的特质。所以，这种理念似乎正在经历一个极其缓慢的渗透过程。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Uh, but I guess that, um, part of the problem is that they really sort of need to, uh, that other countries need to be sort of convinced that the results are there. The results are there in Ethiopia, if you look in terms of poverty reduction, if you look in terms of cereal output increasing three to four times.
transcript.zh: 但我猜，部分问题在于其他国家需要确凿相信这种成效的存在。从埃塞俄比亚来看，成效确实摆在那里，无论是减贫成果，还是粮食产量增长了三到四倍。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: But it's a question like does that, is that what every African government is looking for? When you get the more traditional African government with the older, the older leaders, is that really what they are interested in? And I don't know.
transcript.zh: 但问题在于，这是不是每个非洲国家政府所追求的目标？当你面对那些由老派领导人掌舵的更传统的非洲政府时，这真的是他们感兴趣的吗？我深表怀疑。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: I think we just have to sort of see what is going to happen going forward, but the context, of course, is that with these much-increased populations and massively bigger cities, leaders are under pressure in Africa now in a way that they just were not before.
transcript.zh: 我认为我们只能对未来的走向拭目以待。但大背景在于，随着人口剧增以及城市规模的大幅扩张，非洲的领导人现在承受着前所未有的压力。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: In the past, Africa really was like the 'Big Easy', you know. The leaders of countries always lived well because they could always skim some aid money or some other money that was coming in, right? Your palace is fine. Your kids are all going to college, wherever.
transcript.zh: 过去在非洲当官简直跟混日子一样轻松。国家领导人总能过得优渥，因为他们总能从涌入的援助资金或其他资金中捞上一笔。住着奢华的宫殿，孩子们也被送到海外名校读书。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Got a lot of money squirrelled away in Switzerland and, yeah.
transcript.zh: 在瑞士银行藏了大把的私房钱，诸如此类。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yeah, but now it's a bit different, right? Now you've got huge numbers of young people who are more educated than their parents were. And, you know, as last year with the tax increases in Kenya, people were absolutely insane when they felt that taxes were being increased not in a fair way.
transcript.zh: 是的，但现在情况有些不同了。如今有大量受教育程度远高于父辈的年轻人。就像去年肯尼亚加税引发的风波，当民众觉得税收增加得不公平时，他们彻底被激怒了。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: So, that's a kind of a long answer, but I think that demographic change and, yeah, the demonstration effects from Ethiopia, from Rwanda, from Benin, they may have further impact going forward.
transcript.zh: 这个回答有点长，但我认为人口结构的变化，以及埃塞俄比亚、卢旺达和贝宁等国的示范效应，在未来可能会产生更深远的影响。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, let's hope so. But, you know, in Ethiopia itself, the developmental vibe that you've talked about really did take hold. I mean, Meles used this phrase that I just looked at, 'hegemony', right? He believed that there was this unthinking and unquestioned part of Ethiopian life which was just this obsession with economic development, in the way that he believed that the same vibe had taken hold in Japan, in Korea, in Taiwan, and in China.
transcript.zh: 但愿如此。不过在埃塞俄比亚本土，你谈到的那种发展氛围确实扎下根来。梅莱斯用了我刚查过的一个词——“霸权”（hegemony）。他认为埃塞俄比亚人的生活中曾存在一种不假思索、毋庸置疑的状态，那就是对经济发展的执念；正如他坚信在日本、韩国、中国台湾和中国大陆也曾形成过同样的氛围。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You have an anecdote in there which I thought was just really amusing about how, you know, Taiwanese customs officers took bribes on consumer imports. You're going to import cases of whiskey, they'll take a bribe on it, but not on capital equipment. That was his illustration of developmental hegemony, right? I thought that was very marvelous.
transcript.zh: 你在书中讲过一个我觉得很有趣的轶事：台湾海关官员会对进口消费品受贿，比如你要进口几箱威士忌，他们会收受贿赂，但对资本设备绝不受贿。这就是他对“发展型霸权”的阐释，对吧？我觉得这个例子非常精妙。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: He also, though, of course, uses this to challenge what he calls 'bedtime stories' that link growth to democracy. The American telling of the story is that civil and political rights have to come first, and development will only flow from ensuring those. Chinese listeners will recognize all of this. You yourself use this phrase that's very in favor in China: 'performance legitimacy'. And you say it came most recently from China.
transcript.zh: 当然，他也借此质疑了那些将经济增长与民主制度绑定的所谓“枕边故事”。美国叙事总认为公民权利和政治权利必须先行，经济发展只有在保障这些权利后才会随之而来。中国听众对此必然非常熟悉。你自己也用了在中国备受推崇的表述——“绩效合法性”，并提到这个概念最近正是源自中国。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I guess Ethiopia did arrive at this kind of developmental hegemony. How much of it, in Meles's later years, was more about mainland China rather than Korea or Taiwan? How much was he interested in the PRC by the end?
transcript.zh: 看来埃塞俄比亚确实达成了某种发展型霸权。在梅莱斯晚年，这种理念在多大程度上更多是转向中国大陆，而非韩国或台湾？到最后，他对中国大陆的关注度究竟有多高？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: The evidence that I've looked at and based...
transcript.zh: 根据我所掌握的证据……

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: basing this quite a lot on reading his master's thesis, which I got a copy of from one of his colleagues, the emphasis there is really on South Korea and Taiwan, right? If you go through the bibliography.
transcript.zh: 从我读过他的硕士论文来看——我是从他的一位同事那里拿到副本的——那篇论文的重点其实完全放在了韩国和中国台湾身上，只要你翻阅文后的参考文献就能看出来。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: But that may be partly a question of timing, because those Taiwanese and South Korean case studies have been written up by lots of good authors at the point at which he was in the bush and reading stuff, whereas China was not even really on the map until the early '90s when he goes into government.
transcript.zh: 但这在一定程度上可能是时机问题，因为当他还在打游击、在丛林里读书时，许多优秀学者就已经对中国台湾和韩国的案例进行了详尽研究。而直到90年代初他执政时，中国的发展经验甚至都还没有引起足够关注。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And then in the 2000s, the last decade of his life, as you say, he got more involved in this whole issue of whether democracy is necessary to development. I don't know why he did that, really. I mean, I tend to prefer Amartya Sen's take on that, that these are two completely different things and they're both important, and they're not really related, and it's not helpful to try and relate them. But that doesn't mean that political pluralism isn't something you should seek.
transcript.zh: 到了2000年代，也就是他生命的最后十年，正如你所说，他更加深入地卷入了关于‘民主是否为发展所必需’的争论。我真不知道他为什么非要纠结于此。我个人其实更认同阿马蒂亚·森（Amartya Sen）的观点：这两者是完全不同的维度，并且都极其重要，它们之间并没有直接因果关系，硬要把它们绑在一起毫无益处。但这绝不意味着政治多元化就不是值得追求的目标。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Sure. I mean, there are places, though, where Ethiopia very clearly departs from the Asian script, and in your book you identify two of these. The first is METEC, that's these nine, I think, military businesses that are rolled into a conglomerate in 2011. They handed all ten sugar mill contracts, no tender, just turn them over.
transcript.zh: 确实。不过，埃塞俄比亚在某些方面显然偏离了东亚模式，你在书中也指出了两点。第一点就是METEC（金属工程公司），我记得是由大约九家军工企业在2011年整合而成的一个大型集团。他们甚至未公开招标，就直接拿下了全部十座糖厂的合同。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And, I mean, he turned to North Korea for sugar technology, insisting on being the full engineering contractor for the Grand Renaissance Dam. He's clearly looking at this kind of Korean chaebol model, but he built them in the public sector.
transcript.zh: 我是说，他甚至转向朝鲜获取制糖技术，并坚持由METEC全权承担复兴大坝的总工程总包。他显然是在仿效韩国的财阀（chaebol）模式，却把这种模式建在了公共部门内部。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And then, I think you criticized him for not having given them any competition, where you contrast this with China is that China's answer to this was—this is in the '90s and going further—it wasn't privatization, but it was like to split these state monopolies into competing firms, as they did with telecoms, right? They created, it wasn't all under China Telecom alone, Unicom and then China Mobile were split out, and they were expressly competitive with one another.
transcript.zh: 而且你批评了他没有给这些企业引入任何竞争。你将其与中国做了对比：中国在90年代及随后的解决方式并不是私有化，而是将这些国家垄断行业拆分为互有竞争的企业，电信行业就是典型例子，对吧？中国没有让中国电信一家独大，而是拆分出了中国联通和中国移动，并明确让它们相互竞争。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: The second big departure, I mean just so then we can address both of these, was this leap into the mega projects. And doing this again, maybe he could have looked a little more closely at the Chinese model, which involved small-scale experimentation first, right? You don't just start right away with such enormous scale. Why did he miss these two lessons?
transcript.zh: 第二大偏离——顺便提出来我们可以一起讨论——就是盲目跃进大型超级工程。在这一点上，他本可以更仔细地借鉴中国模式，即先进行小规模试点试验，对吧？你不可能一开始就直接铺开这么庞大的规模。他为什么会忽视这两条教训呢？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: A kind of died-in-the-wool Marxist. Is it his Marxist inheritance? Is it... is it military interests? Um is it something about, you know, how the Asian experience gets read from other geographies? What... what... what went wrong in those cases with METEC?
transcript.zh: 这种彻头彻尾的马克思主义者倾向？这是因为他的马克思主义思想遗产吗？还是军方利益在作祟？又或者是因为其他地区对亚洲经验的解读方式出了偏差？埃塞俄比亚金属工程公司（METEC）到底在哪些方面走偏了？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yeah, I mean it's it's very hard to understand because if you look at his thesis and you look at his bibliography, and then you're trying to think, "Well, how did he fail to understand that competition and private sector were important in Taiwan and South Korea?" So, you know, and he's he's he's he's passed away in 2012, so we can't ask him that.
transcript.zh: 是的，这确实很难理解，因为如果看他的论文和参考书目，你就会纳闷：“他怎么会没看明白，竞争和私营部门在台湾地区和韩国是至关重要的呢？”当然，他已经在2012年去世了，我们也没法当面问他。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: But I, I mean, he just missed those things. The government now, the new government since 2019 is trying to correct for those things. Actually, METEC that you mentioned has been split now into four different bits.
transcript.zh: 但我认为他确实忽视了这些。现在的政府，即2019年上台的新一届政府，正试图纠正这些偏差。事实上，你提到的METEC现在已经被拆分成了四个不同的实体。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And I, I don't know, I mean, if you try and compare with China, is it perhaps a bit like if Deng Xiaoping had been the intellectual resource for the entire Communist Party as well as its leader? That was a bit what it was like with Meles, you know. He was...
transcript.zh: 我也不清楚，如果拿中国来作类比，这大概就类似于邓小平不仅是党内最高领导人，还是整个共产党唯一的思想智库？梅莱斯（Meles Zenawi）当时差不多就是这种状态。他……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, it's a big ask, yeah.
transcript.zh: 是啊，这要求未免太高了。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: He was so intellectually dominant that I'm not sure it was necessarily a good thing for... I mean, he had the right basic ideas, but I think it was very hard to challenge him. And yeah, that's why... yeah, that's why some mistakes were certainly made.
transcript.zh: 他在智识上太有压倒性了，以至于我不确定这究竟是不是一件好事……我的意思是，他宏观的大方向是对的，但我认为别人极难去挑战他的观点。是的，这正是一系列失误在所难免的原因。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, the Ethiopia chapter's harshest judgment is really about the constitution itself, the federal constitution of 1995, which, you know, defines these nine ethnic states, all of them with an actual constitutional right to secession. Your ethnicity is printed on your identity card. States choose their own language, their own curricula.
transcript.zh: 对，埃塞俄比亚这章最严厉的批判，实际上针对的是其宪法本身——1995年的联邦宪法。这部宪法划分了九个民族邦，而且每个邦在宪法层面上都拥有合法的分离脱离权。身份证上赫然印着你的民族属性，各邦可以自主选择官方语言和教学大纲。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: This is all just basically so that a Tigrayan elite, you know, it's just 6% of the population, they're really in charge of this multi-ethnic federation from behind the curtain. You have an Ethiopian-American businessman tell you in the book flatly, "Federalism is the problem." And you seem largely to agree with that.
transcript.zh: 而这一切的根本目的，基本上是为了让仅占总人口6%的提格雷精英能够在幕后牢牢掌控这个多民族联邦。你在书中提到一位埃塞俄比亚裔美国商人直截了当地告诉你：“联邦制才是问题的根源。”而你似乎也大体认同这一点。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Even this character in the book, Arkebe Oqubay, the architect of the industrial strategy, he basically talks about how, yeah, the federal system forced him to disperse these industrial parks to places that just made no economic sense at all, right?
transcript.zh: 甚至书中提到的工业战略设计师阿尔克贝·奥库拜（Arkebe Oqubay），他也谈到联邦制度如何迫使他把这些工业园区分散到完全不符合经济理性的偏远地方，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: There's one where, in... I don't know the geography of Ethiopia well, but apparently Jimma, where there's one, and the only sensible thing to make is wood products, but here he's doing steel-based stuff. So is... is federalism the problem, Joe?
transcript.zh: 比如有一个地方——我不太熟悉埃塞俄比亚的地理，但好像是在吉马（Jimma）——建了园区，当地唯一合理的产业本应是木制品加工，但他们却硬要搞钢铁相关的重工产业。所以，联邦制真的是病根所在吗，Joe？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yes, I think... I think it has been because, I mean, I think you've either got to go all in on federalism...
transcript.zh: 是的，我认为……我认为它确实一直是病根所在。因为在我看来，搞联邦制你要么就贯彻到底……

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: You know, I would say what's been more successful, perhaps, is the way the Nigerians have developed their federalism. Although it started off with a civil war that killed a million people in '67-'68, Nigeria started off with only three regions.
transcript.zh: 要我说，尼日利亚发展联邦制的方式或许相对更成功一些。尽管它最初也是始于1967至1968年一场导致百万人丧生的内战，当时尼日利亚仅由三个大区组成。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: So they got in a civil war in the late '60s, and over the years, it's moved to now 36 different states. And the idea being that if you make them smaller, they're less able to make trouble, and it kind of has worked.
transcript.zh: 因此他们在60年代末爆发了内战。多年来，各州不断拆分，如今已有36个州。其逻辑在于，如果把州划得更小，它们掀起大风浪的能力就会减弱，事实证明这确实在一定程度上起到了作用。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Ethiopia had a situation where it had some larger regions, but it had different ethnic groups spilling over borders and people living with each other. What the constitution of the early '90s did was to require defined boundaries.
transcript.zh: 埃塞俄比亚的情况则是，它原本有一些较大的区域，但各族群犬牙交错、跨界混居。而90年代初宪法的做法，是要求划定明确的边界。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: So once you require defined boundaries, you've sort of said, 'Right, this is our place, and that's your place.' And all of the ethnic cleansing that has happened since has been on the basis of sort of getting people to go back into their defined areas.
transcript.zh: 一旦要求划清界限，就等于是在宣布：“好，这是我们的地界，那是你们的地界。”此后发生的所有种族清洗，基本都是打着让人们“退回各自划定区域”的旗号进行的。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And then, as you say, people were allowed to have their local language for education and also as a second language for government. And really all it did, the federal system in Ethiopia, was to make people have stronger state identities, stronger ethnic identity.
transcript.zh: 而且正如你所说，人们被允许在教育中使用当地族语，并将其作为政府的第二工作语言。埃塞俄比亚这套联邦制所产生的一切实际效果，无非就是强化了人们的邦州认同与族群认同。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Right. Regionalism.
transcript.zh: 对，地方主义。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And that has just not been a positive thing for Ethiopia, and it's stoked violence which is going on at the time. But, you know, at the heart of it all was the fact that the biggest con in the whole federal system was that the Tigrayans, who were only 6% of the population, always retained control of the army, control of the security service, and control of politics from sort of behind the curtain.
transcript.zh: 这对埃塞俄比亚来说绝非幸事，反而助长了彼时至今延绵不绝的暴力冲突。但归根结底，整个联邦制度最大的骗局在于：仅占总人口6%的提格雷人，始终牢牢掌控着军队、安全部门，并在幕后操纵着国家政治。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: So that was always going to cause trouble. And in 2020, we had this spiral into this horrific civil war, which killed perhaps 600,000 people.
transcript.zh: 因此这迟早会酿成祸端。到了2020年，局势急转直下，演变成一场惨烈至极的内战，夺走了大约60万人的生命。
