transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Right. I mean, now, you know, in the parts of Ethiopia that are safe—which is by no means all parts, but in the parts that are safe—the country is very much back to business.
transcript.zh: 不过话说回来，如今在埃塞俄比亚那些安全的地区——虽绝非全国皆安，但在安全地带——这个国家基本重回正轨。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Back on track, yeah.
transcript.zh: 重回正轨了，是的。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yeah, yeah, growing 10% again this year.
transcript.zh: 没错，今年经济增速又达到了10%。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: One of the striking things in your book for me was this anecdote that Hailemariam told you. In September 2013, at the G20 back in St. Petersburg—that's a distant memory now—it was just six months after Xi Jinping took power, the two of them are sitting in a hotel executive lounge...
transcript.zh: 你书中让我印象极为深刻的一处细节，是 Hailemariam 对你讲的一段轶事。那是在2013年9月圣彼得堡的二十国集团（G20）峰会上——如今回想起来已恍如隔世——当时习近平刚掌权六个月，他们两人正坐在酒店行政酒廊里……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Xi Jinping says to him, to Hailemariam, 'I'm worried about Ethiopia. Why don't you become one party? Why have you had regional parties for this long period of time?' And Hailemariam tells you, you know, 'Look, I couldn't answer him.'
transcript.zh: 习近平对他说，也就是对 Hailemariam 说：“我很担心埃塞俄比亚。你们为什么不合并成一个党呢？为什么这么长时间以来一直搞地方政党？”Hailemariam 告诉你，“你看，我当时根本回答不上来。”

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So, seven years later, as you say, the country is in this horrific war. How did Hailemariam tell that story to you? Was it like more of a confession? Was it a kind of a vindication of Xi, this idea that you have to have a centralized unitary state, otherwise you can't, you know, 'let some people get rich faster', like Deng exhorted?
transcript.zh: 七年后，正如你所说，这个国家爆发了可怕的战争。Hailemariam 是怎么向你讲述这个故事的？这更像是一种忏悔吗？还是对习近平的一种认可——即必须建立一个中央集权的单一制国家，否则就无法像邓小平倡导的那样“让一部分人先富起来”？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: What did you make of that? You had a Chinese leader...
transcript.zh: 对此你怎么看？一位中国领导人……

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yeah, I was struck by him telling me the story. He was in this very difficult position as premier because the Tigrayans basically put him in as premier when Meles died.
transcript.zh: 是的，他跟我讲这个故事时我也很吃惊。他当时作为总理处境极其艰难，因为在梅莱斯去世后，基本上是提格雷人推举他当总理的。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: He was from a very small ethnic group in the south of Ethiopia, so he had no meaningful political constituency backing him. He was a technocrat really, and he did the best that he could, but in the end he stepped down as prime minister because he was just so heavily manipulated, and there was also so much civil strife in the country.
transcript.zh: 他来自埃塞俄比亚南部一个非常小的族群，因此背后没有真正有分量的政治选民群体支持他。他本质上是个技术官僚，尽了最大努力，但最终还是辞去了总理职务，因为他受制于人太深，而且国内还发生了严重的内乱。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: What he said about that conversation with Xi Jinping came out of a conversation between us with me just trying to understand how they had gotten into this situation in the first place. But as you mentioned, Meles Zenawi's background was that of a Marxist intellectual.
transcript.zh: 他提到与习近平的那次谈话，源于我们当时的一次交流，我只是想弄明白他们最初究竟是如何陷入这种局面的。但正如你所提到的，梅莱斯·泽纳维的背景是一位马克思主义知识分子。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Basically what Meles Zenawi was trying to do in Ethiopia was what Tito did in Yugoslavia or Stalin did in Russia. It was that model of kind of fake federalism.
transcript.zh: 梅莱斯·泽纳维在埃塞俄比亚试图推行的，基本上就是铁托在南斯拉夫或斯大林在俄罗斯所做的那套。那就是一种徒有其表的联邦制模式。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So this brings us, of course, to the Prosperity Party. Abiy, when he comes to power, folds the Amhara, Oromo, and southern parties into this single non-ethnic organization at the end of 2019, but the Tigrayans refuse to join.
transcript.zh: 这就把我们带到了繁荣党的话题上。阿比在2019年底上台后，将阿姆哈拉、奥罗莫以及南方的各政党整合进这个非民族性的单一组织，但提格雷人拒绝加入。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You write how the model that Abiy has in mind at this time is the LDP, Japan's LDP. It's a big tent. It's governed Japan since the end of the war for all but a handful of years, six years I think, by accommodating factions rather than suppressing them, right? I guess that's the... so you have very left-leaning and very right-leaning LDP members.
transcript.zh: 你写到阿比当时心目中的模板是日本自民党。它是一个“大帐篷”政党，战后除短短几年（好像是六年）外一直执政，其方式是包容各派系而非打压派系，对吧？我想这就是……所以自民党内部既有极其偏左的成员，也有极其偏右的成员。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So can Ethiopia build an LDP?
transcript.zh: 那么埃塞俄比亚能建立起自民党这样的模式吗？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: It's a good question, Kaiser, but I don't have an answer. But I think they've moved in the right direction. I think they've got to go away from formal federalism to the Prosperity Party.
transcript.zh: 问得好，Kaiser，但我没有确切的答案。不过我认为他们的大方向是对的。我认为他们必须摆脱形式上的联邦制，走向繁荣党模式。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And you know, on the face of it, it's a non-ethnic party, but of course people will look at it and say, "No, it's not a non-ethnic party. It's now a bunch of Oromo running the government, because before we had the Tigrayans."
transcript.zh: 表面上看，这是一个非族裔政党，但人们显然会审视并指出：“不，这根本不是什么非族裔政党。以前是提格雷人掌权，现在换成了一帮奥罗莫人统治政府。”

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And you know, the Oromo want their day in the sun because they constitute 34% of the population. They are the biggest bloc.
transcript.zh: 而且奥罗莫人也渴望迎来属于自己的扬眉吐气之日，因为他们占了总人口的34%，是最大的族群力量。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: So, yeah, I mean it's difficult, it's really difficult, and this is where we sort of separate so clearly from East Asia. We don't separate from everywhere in Southeast Asia, but if we look at East Asia and we look at Japan and Korea and China, and then in economic terms, I would include Vietnam.
transcript.zh: 所以，这确实非常棘手。这也正是非洲与东亚截然不同的地方。东南亚某些地方可能并非如此，但纵观东亚，看看日本、韩国、中国，从经济角度我还会算上越南。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: You know, the commonality is that the ethnic minority populations are 5% or less. So, it's nothing, right? So, you know, "I'm a Han, you're a Han, everybody's a Han" kind of thing, and we can all go forward with our economic development.
transcript.zh: 它们的共同点在于少数民族人口比例都在5%以下。几乎可以忽略不计，对吧？于是就成了“我是汉族，你也是汉族，大家都是汉族”这种状态，所有人都能心无旁骛地推进经济发展。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And it makes it much easier to have an authoritarian government, yeah? In China, the polling tells us that people are quite happy, you know, so long as they feel that they're becoming better off. A bit less happy now perhaps, but they have been quite happy over the years.
transcript.zh: 这使得建立威权政府变得容易得多。在中国，民调显示，只要人们觉得自己生活在变好，他们就相当满足。现在或许没那么满意了，但多年来他们整体上一直很满意。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: To have an authoritarian government because, you know, well, whatever. We just get on with our lives and we are seeing income growth.
transcript.zh: 对于威权政府统治无所谓，反正大家只管过好自己的日子，而且收入确实在不断增长。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: But these options are just not available in Africa. And the reason again, to me, is the traditional low population density.
transcript.zh: 但非洲根本没有这种选择余地。在我看来，原因依然在于其历史上长期的低人口密度。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Because what the historical consensus about Africa, which is not supported by very hard evidence because there are almost no written records in most societies, but what historians think is that because Africa was so sparsely populated, many ethnic—to use a very loose term—groups were just 10,000 people or 15,000 people.
transcript.zh: 因为关于非洲的历史共识——虽然缺乏极其确凿的证据支撑，毕竟大多数本土社会几乎没有文字记载——但历史学家认为，正因为非洲人口极其稀疏，很多族群（宽泛而言）规模往往只有一万到一万五千人。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Traditionally, there wasn't a lot of conflict in Africa because when you butted up against another group, you could always go off and find another area, new land to live in. And so you get, you know, a couple of thousand different ethnic groups surviving in Africa, which is very unlike East Asia.
transcript.zh: 传统上非洲并没有发生太多冲突，因为当你与其他族群发生摩擦时，大可以迁徙到另一片无主土地定居。因此，非洲延续保留了数千个不同的族群，这与东亚迥然不同。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And this means that in terms of your economic development, you're always contending with this ethnic fragmentation. And that makes the politics much harder than it has been in East Asia, and we just have to see how things develop.
transcript.zh: 这就意味着，在推进经济发展时，你必须时刻应对这种族群撕裂。这导致非洲的政治运作比东亚要艰难复杂得多，未来走向仍有待观察。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: You'll remember I make the point in the four countries that I look at in greatest detail in the book, that I say that each of them actually was also characterized by a cross-ethnic coalition at the start.
transcript.zh: 你会记得，我在书中重点详述的四个国家中强调过一个观点：它们每一个在起步之初，实际上也都具备跨族群联盟的特征。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: That's right.
transcript.zh: 没错。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: of their progress. So they, oddly enough, they all—well, it's not odd, I suppose—but they all confronted the ethnic fragmentation problem at the beginning.
transcript.zh: 他们取得进展的先决条件。因此，说来也奇怪——其实想想也不奇怪——他们在一开始都正面解决了族群割裂的问题。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Whereas most African states so far haven't really confronted it, although others are sort of moving in that that direction. I mean...
transcript.zh: 而大多数非洲国家迄今尚未真正去面对这一问题，尽管其他一些国家正在朝这个方向发展。我是说……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Nigeria, would you say? Yeah.
transcript.zh: 你觉得尼日利亚算吗？是的。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yeah, and in a way, we kind of have that in South Africa now, where the sort of ANC is in decline, but now ruling in tandem with the Democratic Alliance, which has a bigger white constituency, I think.
transcript.zh: 是的，在某种程度上南非现在也呈现出这种态势：非国大（ANC）日渐式微，目前正与拥有更多白人选民基础的民主联盟联合执政。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So, you characterize the war, of course, like you said, a half million people dead, most of them from starvation and disease. It's the biggest developmental tragedy in Africa for a generation. It's hard not to agree.
transcript.zh: 正如你所描述的那场战争，造成了整整50万人死亡，其中大部分死于饥荒和疾病。这是非洲一代人以来面临的最大发展悲剧，这点确实毋庸置疑。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: But clearly, the economy did not collapse. As you say, agriculture is back, growing faster actually during the war than in the decade before it. Debt actually drops during the period of the war. The big dam got finished.
transcript.zh: 但显然，经济并没有崩溃。正如你所说，农业恢复了，战争期间的增速甚至超过了战前十年；债务在战争期间反倒下降了；那座大型水坝也完工了。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So, you ask, as the title of your chapter, "Is this dream destroyed or delayed?" And it seems you come down on simply having been delayed, right? Since you finished writing, as you just said, they're back to double-digit growth. They've got a new IMF program. Things are looking up, yeah?
transcript.zh: 所以，正如你那一章的标题所问：“这场梦想是破灭了还是推迟了？”你似乎倾向于认为只是被推迟了，对吧？在你写完书后，正如你刚才所说，他们重新恢复了两位数增长，还获得了IMF的新贷款项目，形势正在好转，是吧？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yeah, I mean, there's a lot to be positive about. The new government has made changes that allow more space for the private sector. They seem to understand the need for competition.
transcript.zh: 是的，我的意思是，有很多值得乐观的地方。新政府推行了一些改革，为私营部门腾出了更多空间。他们似乎也理解竞争的必要性。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: They've got World Bank and IMF loans at very low rates of interest, which sort out the debt problem that they previously had. So, yeah.
transcript.zh: 他们以极低的利率获得了世界银行和IMF的贷款，化解了此前背负的债务危机。所以，确实如此。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: I mean, and as you say, something like the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, with more than three gigawatts of power coming from it, that got finished, and...
transcript.zh: 而且正如你所说，像复兴大坝这样装机容量超过3吉瓦的项目已经竣工，并且……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: They're exporting power now, yeah.
transcript.zh: 他们现在已经开始出口电力了，对吧。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yeah, they're selling power to Sudan, to Kenya, to Tanzania, to Djibouti. So, um...
transcript.zh: 是的，他们正在向苏丹、肯尼亚、坦桑尼亚和吉布提输送电力。所以，嗯……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Joe, let me ask you specifically about China's part in the Ethiopian story, since you saw a good deal of it on the ground there. I don't know if you've seen this remarkable film called 'Made in Ethiopia' from 2024?
transcript.zh: Joe，我想具体问问中国在埃塞俄比亚的发展历程中扮演了什么角色，因为你在当地实地见证了许多。不知道你有没有看过2024年那部引人瞩目的纪录片《Made in Ethiopia》？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Oh, no, I haven't.
transcript.zh: 噢，还没有，我没看过。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Oh, it's wonderful. It's directed by this guy named Max Duncan and Xinyan Yu. Duncan was an ex-Reuters video guy, and Xinyan Yu was this... I actually worked with her before for a little while on a documentary that I did for PBS's long-running science series 'NOVA'. But she's very talented.
transcript.zh: 拍得太棒了。导演是Max Duncan和Xinyan Yu（于新艳）。Duncan之前是路透社的视频记者，而于新艳——我之前在为PBS老牌科学系列节目《NOVA》拍纪录片时曾和她共事过一段时间，她非常有才华。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It's great. You got to check it out. I won't spoil it for you, but it's kind of an observational documentary. There's no talking heads or narration, and it just follows this Chinese industrial park...
transcript.zh: 片子非常棒，你一定要看看。我就不剧透了，它是一部观察式的纪录片，没有受访者对着镜头的“大头照”，也没有旁白解说，只是镜头一路跟拍一个中国产业园区……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: in Dukem, about 35 miles or so, or kilometers, I guess, southeast of Addis. It's this big Chinese-run industrial park, and you know, it has all the, it takes place against the backdrop of, you know, the war and everything, so it's really very good. Highly recommend it.
transcript.zh: 杜肯距离亚的斯亚贝巴东南约35英里，或者说是35公里。那里是一个大型的中国运营工业园区。影片以战争等事件为背景展开，拍得非常出色，强烈推荐。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Anyway, I mean I was asking you, right? So, you know, when you look at that film, you see a lot of evidence of China. You know, there's still Chinese characters on the doors of the light rail that they built.
transcript.zh: 总之，我之前想问你的是，当你看这部片子时，能看到大量中国的印记。比如他们修建的轻轨车门上，至今还留有汉字。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It's, you know, there's thousands of kilometers of road that are done with, you know, Chinese tenders. But they seem to have done a couple of things right, like there wasn't a large-scale import of Chinese labor that you saw, like in Kenya with the Standard Gauge Railway.
transcript.zh: 还有成千上万公里的道路是通过中国公司中标承建的。但他们似乎做对了几件事，比如并没有像肯尼亚蒙内标准轨铁路那样大规模输入中国劳工。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: China ended up having, what, about $14 billion in loans, but they've agreed to restructure them. Chinese contractors were the ones to, you know, kind of come in and fix the problems with the sugar mills. There's a lot of other stuff where China shows up.
transcript.zh: 中国最终提供了大约140亿美元的贷款，但他们已经同意进行债务重组。也是中国承包商介入，解决了那些糖厂的问题。中国在许多其他领域也都有身影。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Can you talk a little bit about what the Chinese relationship looks like today from Addis and how the Ethiopians seem to have managed it in, I think, generally a laudable way?
transcript.zh: 你能否谈谈从亚的斯亚贝巴的角度来看，如今中埃关系是怎样的？埃塞俄比亚人又是如何以一种我认为总体上值得赞许的方式来处理这种关系的？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yeah, I mean, I think, you know, China has obviously been important. Ethiopia was the second biggest borrower from China in Africa after Angola. And big loans included the rail line up to Djibouti, which has had some sort of teething problems, but seems to be working okay now.
transcript.zh: 是的，中国的作用显然举足轻重。埃塞俄比亚是非洲仅次于安哥拉的第二大对华借款国。巨额贷款项目包括通往吉布提的铁路线，虽然经历了一些磨合期的问题，但现在运转良好。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And obviously, in Ethiopia, the engagement with China reflects the broad change in the Belt and Road Initiative, which, up until, so from 2013, where Xi Jinping comes in, through to about 2020, it's all about policy bank lending, usually for infrastructure projects.
transcript.zh: 显而易见，埃塞俄比亚与中国的互动折射出了“一带一路”倡议的广泛转型。从2013年习近平上台到2020年左右，该倡议主要以政策性银行贷款为主，通常用于基础设施项目。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: So that would be something like the Modjo-Addis to Djibouti rail line to take manufactured goods out and bring Ethiopia's imports in. But then, since then, it's important to understand that it's changed in as much as there's still plenty of Chinese credit available in Africa, but it's now coming from Chinese commercial banks, and it's coming from syndicated loans, which are led by Chinese commercial banks.
transcript.zh: 比如莫焦/亚的斯亚贝巴至吉布提的铁路，就是用来运出工业制成品并运入埃塞俄比亚所需的进口物资。但从那之后，必须理解的是情况发生了变化：尽管非洲仍能获得充裕的中国信贷，但如今这些资金主要来自中国的商业银行，以及由中国商业银行牵头的银团贷款。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Right.
transcript.zh: 对。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And the numbers that I've seen suggest that actually the amount of money coming in is bigger than ever in the last two, three years. And it's also moving now to focus more on manufacturing.
transcript.zh: 而且我看到的数据表明，过去两三年里涌入的资金规模其实比以往任何时候都要大。并且资金的投向正转向更多聚焦于制造业。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Really, like the last sort of three years, there's a number of different sources on manufacturing, but if you, they roughly agree that last year Chinese firms, if we think of FDI now rather than the lending, that Chinese...
transcript.zh: 实际上在过去的三年左右，关于制造业投资有若干不同的数据来源，但大致都吻合：去年中国企业——如果我们现在考虑的是外商直接投资（FDI）而非借贷的话——中国……

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Chinese firms put about $12 billion into manufacturing in Africa, and that's a big change from three-plus years ago when it was much more resources-focused.
transcript.zh: 中国企业在非洲制造业投资了约120亿美元，这与三年多前相比是个巨大的转变，当时投资更多集中在资源领域。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, very extractive-focused, yeah.
transcript.zh: 是的，非常侧重于资源开采，没错。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: So all that's important. I mean, I was in Addis, I don't know, 2 months ago, and going around Addis, there are lots of Chinese projects underway. Most of what I saw, I think, were private sector projects that have been done or overseen.
transcript.zh: 所以这些都很重要。大概两个月前我去过亚的斯亚贝巴，在城里转的时候，能看到大量正在推进的中国项目。据我观察，其中大部分似乎都是已经落成或正在监管的私营部门项目。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: As you say, in Ethiopia projects will get managed by Chinese firms, but the labor, the kind of ordinary labor, is not Chinese. That doesn't happen.
transcript.zh: 正如你所说，在埃塞俄比亚，项目会由中国公司管理，但劳动力——也就是普通劳工，绝不是中国人。这种情况并不存在。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And the biggest one, the biggest one that I saw is the new airport at Bishoftu, which has 6,000 trucks going day and night, just establishing the terrain at the moment for that. And that is being managed by two Chinese firms. China Road and Bridge is one, and I can't remember the other one.
transcript.zh: 我见过的最大工程是位于比绍夫图的新机场，目前有六千辆卡车日夜不停地运载作业，光是前期平整场地。该项目由两家中国企业负责管理，其中一家是中国路桥，另一家我记不太清了。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Anyway, so there's lots going on. Chinese firms are still doing lots of stuff, lots of stuff, but it's much more in the private sector. It's much more driven by Chinese commercial banks.
transcript.zh: 总之，那里的建设如火如荼。中国企业依然在推进大量业务，但现在更多属于私营领域，也更多是由中国商业银行驱动的。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And in my experience, Chinese people quite like being in Africa. And I'm always struck about how sort of cosmopolitan they are in the sense of learning local languages and things. I mean, you know, learning Arabic. In Rwanda, I saw with a woman who, then I said, "Oh, do you speak Kinyarwanda?" "Oh yeah, very well." And who speak Amharic in Ethiopia.
transcript.zh: 而且据我的观察，中国人其实挺喜欢待在非洲的。他们的开放与世界主义倾向经常让我感到惊讶，比如去主动学习当地语言等。有人学阿拉伯语；在卢旺达，我遇到过一位女士，我问她：“你会说卢旺达语吗？”她说：“会啊，说得很流利。”在埃塞俄比亚也有人会讲阿姆哈拉语。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: So, yeah, I think, you know, I always think of China as a cosmopolitan country. And when you see Chinese people in somewhere like Ethiopia, that plays out.
transcript.zh: 所以，我一直认为中国是一个具有全球包容视野的国家。当你看到在埃塞俄比亚等地的中国人时，这种特质就体现得淋漓尽致。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: It's not to say that there aren't occasional, you know, there aren't sometimes disagreements. I mean, you mentioned the light rail system. And I know that the Ethiopian government is now furious inasmuch as they weren't told by the Chinese contractors on the light rail that it can't take more cars because the way that the rails were set up means that it can't support additional weight.
transcript.zh: 这并不是说双方就完全没有摩擦。你刚才提到了轻轨系统，据我所知，埃塞俄比亚政府现在对此非常不满，因为中国轻轨承包商之前并未告知他们轨道无法增加车厢——轨道的铺设规格决定了它无法承受更多重量。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: So, of course, they've got a full train, and they assumed they could add more cars to it, and they can't. So they're not very happy about that.
transcript.zh: 结果就是列车挤得水泄不通，他们本以为能加挂车厢，实际却行不通。因此他们对此颇有微词。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I haven't followed that. That's interesting. But, yeah, this kind of warms my heart and what you say about this cosmopolitanism on the part of the Chinese in Africa, that is very positive.
transcript.zh: 这事我还真没关注过，挺有意思的。不过，你刚才提到中国人在非洲展现出的这种世界主义胸怀，确实让人感到欣慰，非常积极正面。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You end your chapter on this idea that you've already flicked at, the "demonstration effect." You quote Alice Amsden's argument that East Asia had Japan to sort of show the way. Africa and Latin America have languished for want of a local model.
transcript.zh: 你在该章结尾再次探讨了你之前提及的“示范效应”。你引用了 Alice Amsden 的观点，指出东亚有日本在前面引路，而非洲和拉美则因缺乏本土样板而步履维艰。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And you write that, you know, the continent desperately needs Ethiopia to get back on track. Is there any sign so far...
transcript.zh: 你写道，整个非洲大陆迫切需要埃塞俄比亚重回正轨。到目前为止，是否有什么迹象表明……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You've seen that other African governments were watching Ethiopia the way, say, Korea watched Japan, or that Vietnam has paid very close attention to China. Who was taking notes and, now that the war is done, is the model discredited, or is it just the politics maybe that have been discredited? Is Ethiopia having this demonstration effect?
transcript.zh: 你是否注意到其他非洲国家政府也在关注埃塞俄比亚，就像韩国当年关注日本，或是越南高度关注中国那样？有谁在认真汲取经验？如今内战结束，这一模式是声誉扫地了，还是说声誉受损的只是其政治层面？换言之，埃塞俄比亚是否产生了这种示范效应？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yeah. I don't think that the relationship is ever going to be quite what Korea was with Japan, because, of course, Japan had colonized Korea. So there were all sorts of people who'd been in the Japanese colonial army who were in Korean government after independence, and even though they didn't like the Japanese, the learning was kind of embedded.
transcript.zh: 是的。我认为这种关系永远不可能完全像韩日之间那样，因为日本曾殖民过韩国。因此，韩国独立后政府中有大量曾在日本殖民地军队服役的人，即便他们不喜欢日本人，但那种学习和借鉴是根深蒂固的。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: With Ethiopia, it's a funny sort of relationship, because Abiy's done this as well. They tend to, from time to time, say, "Oh, we're not really African," which doesn't make them many friends.
transcript.zh: 至于埃塞俄比亚，这种关系就显得有些微妙了，因为阿比也常这么干。他们往往时不时会流露出一种“噢，我们算不上真正意义上的非洲人”的心态，这可没法让他们广交朋友。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: So, but nonetheless, you can't help seeing what is going on in Ethiopia when you go to Addis. And, of course, everybody has to go to Addis because that's where the African Union is. So all African leaders see Ethiopia on an ongoing basis.
transcript.zh: 但即便如此，当你去到亚的斯亚贝巴时，你不可能看不到埃塞俄比亚正在发生的变化。当然，所有人都得去亚的斯，因为非盟总部就设在那里。所以所有非洲领导人都会经常看到埃塞俄比亚的现状。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And I think again that probably Abiy—he may not mean it this way, but he's probably having a sort of positive effect on stirring other people up and getting them a bit more serious about policy. Because he also frequently tells Africa and African leaders that Ethiopia will be the biggest economy on the continent by 2050, and that there's absolutely no doubt about this.
transcript.zh: 而且我认为，阿比——尽管他本意或许不在此，但他可能确实起到了积极的刺激作用，激起了其他人的紧迫感，促使他们更严肃地对待政策制定。因为他也经常向全非洲和各国领导人放言，埃塞俄比亚到2050年必将成为非洲大陆第一大经济体，对此毫无悬念。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: It's currently seven, and it's about to overtake Kenya. If it continues to grow at around 10%, it will be number one, but he kind of likes to rub people's faces in that.
transcript.zh: 它目前排在第七位，且即将超过肯尼亚。如果能继续保持10%左右的增速，它确实会跃居第一，但他总爱当面把这话说得让人难堪。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I'm sure he's winning friends with that. Look, I want to ask you the question I've been circling for years. You're really one of the few people I can think of who's positioned to answer it bluntly.
transcript.zh: 那我敢肯定他这么做树敌不少。你看，我想问你一个我琢磨了很多年的问题。在我想得到的人里，你真的是极少数能对此直言不讳的人之一。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So if you strip away what is generically East Asian in China's rise—land reform, although the Chinese version of land reform, of course, was far more highly coercive than what we saw in other East Asian countries, but the export-led manufacturing, the repressed financial system, the closed capital accounts—what is left that is specifically Chinese?
transcript.zh: 如果剥离掉中国崛起中属于泛东亚模式的普遍特征——比如土地改革，尽管中国的土改相比我们在其他东亚国家看到的要暴力和强制得多，但还有出口导向型制造业、金融抑制以及资本账户管制——那么究竟剩下什么是纯粹属于中国特有的？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: In the book, you point to a few things, like this habit of piloting a policy locally before scaling it up nationally, the 1990s fix of...
transcript.zh: 你在书中指出了几点，比如先在地方试点再向全国推广的政策习惯，以及20世纪90年代对……的整顿解决。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Breaking these state monopolies into competing state firms, which we already talked about. Is China just a scaled-up Japan, or Korea, or Taiwan, or is it something different in kind?
transcript.zh: 打破这些国家垄断，拆分为相互竞争的国有企业，这些我们之前已经讨论过了。中国究竟只是一个放大版的日本、韩国或台湾，还是在本质上有所不同？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Well, I mean I would I would say that the basic policies that I set out in in How Asia Works are the are the same. But that doesn't mean that China is just a scaled-up Japan because China built a different government with with slightly different capabilities.
transcript.zh: 嗯，我想说，我在《亚洲模式》（How Asia Works）中阐述的基本政策逻辑是一致的。但这并不意味着中国只是一个放大版的日本，因为中国建立了一套具有略微不同治理能力的独特政府体制。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And as you were saying, you know, managed to do, you know, managed to to to develop capacities whether it is the local testing of policies before a very rapid national roll out, or what Zhu Rongji managed to do in the 90s, where everybody was saying to him, you know, you've got to privatize all these all these state-owned enterprises.
transcript.zh: 正如你刚才所言，中国成功发展出了这些能力——无论是在全国迅速铺开之前先进行地方政策试点，还是朱镕基在90年代所做的那样。当时所有人都对他说，你必须把这些国有企业全部私有化。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And he realized that, no, I don't have to privatize them. What I need is competition. If we get competition, we'll get better performance. And so he usually chopped them into four pieces, and have four four state enterprises compete against each other.
transcript.zh: 但他意识到：不，我没必要把它们私有化。我真正需要的是竞争。只要引入竞争，效益就会提升。所以他通常把它们一分为四，让四家国有企业相互竞争。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: So it was maybe second best in the sense that they would have been even better if they were private, but the party didn't want that. So he kind of kept everybody happy. I mean, he produced massively improved performance, and kept the party happy.
transcript.zh: 所以这或许算是个次优选择，也就是说如果彻底私有化表现可能会更好，但党并不希望那样做。于是他让各方都感到满意——既大幅提升了绩效，又维护了党的诉求。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: So, you know, those all sorts of things like that I think are particularly Chinese moments. Just as without getting into it, I mean certain things that Xi Jinping is doing are probably going to be viewed as particularly Chinese moments.
transcript.zh: 所以，我认为这类举措都是极具中国特色的时刻。正如抛开细节不谈，习近平如今所做的一些事情，可能也会被视为极具中国特色的时刻。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And indeed the general thrust of where he's going with the country is not anywhere that anybody in the situation he inherited has gone after so far. I mean, you know, instead of sort of driving slowly towards increased private ownership and greater pluralism, he's just done a handbrake turn in terms of, you know, how the economy is to be run and controlled.
transcript.zh: 事实上，他引领国家前进的大方向，在以往继承类似局面的领导人中是从未有过的。我是说，他并没有慢慢走向扩大私有制和更多元化的道路，而是在经济的运行与管控方式上直接来了一个急刹车调头。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: So there's, yeah, there's lots that's that's Chinese. But the the basics of why smallholder agriculture works, of why export manufacturing works, and of why there is good reason, if you're capable of doing it, of manipulating your financial system a bit, I think those are the commonalities across these countries.
transcript.zh: 所以，确实有很多独具中国特色的地方。但关于小农农业为何见效、出口导向型制造业为何管用，以及在能力允许的前提下适度调控金融体系为何合情合理，这些基础逻辑在这些国家之间都是共通的。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So Joe, let me ask you to kind of go down the list of major African states and kind of tell me which ones are most like China, in the sense of being able to, you know, run something like its program. I mean, obviously we start with Ethiopia, and it's got a lot of the conditions that, you know, it's actually got the the densely populated highland plateau.
transcript.zh: 那么Joe，我想请你梳理一下主要的非洲国家，告诉我哪些在推行类似发展方案的能力上最像中国？显然我们要先从埃塞俄比亚说起，它具备很多条件，比如确实拥有人口稠密的高原地区。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It looked cheap, you know, in terms of global labor costs. Ethiopia, you know, kept its capital controls that more than, you know, 30 African countries signed away under IMF...
transcript.zh: 在全球劳动力成本方面，它显得极具性价比。埃塞俄比亚保留了资本管制，而超过30个非洲国家在国际货币基金组织（IMF）的要求下已经放弃了这一政策……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Pressure for structural adjustment. But what about, let's just, like Nigeria, Kenya, Tanzania, Egypt, Morocco? What disqualifies the ones that can't do it?
transcript.zh: 结构性调整的压力。但那其他国家呢？比如尼日利亚、肯尼亚、坦桑尼亚、埃及、摩洛哥？究竟是什么原因让那些未能成功的国家掉队了？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Is it what you started off with, demography? Is it the financial architecture? Is it the politics, or the kind of coastal consumption cities that you describe? What's holding the rest back, and which ones, how would you rank them ordinarily in terms of their China-eskness?
transcript.zh: 是因为你一开始提到的人口结构吗？还是金融架构？或者是政治体制，抑或是你所描述的那种沿海消费型城市？到底是什么在阻碍其他国家的发展？如果要按‘与中国模式的相似度’给它们排个序，你会怎么排？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Well, I'm not sure I would say that any are China-esque, because, of course, what we said about ethnic fragmentation, so nothing feels like China because it's all got, you know, loads of different contending groups.
transcript.zh: 我不确定能不能说有哪个国家像中国，因为正如我们之前谈到的族群碎片化问题，非洲没有任何一个地方让人感觉像中国，因为到处都充斥着大量相互博弈的群体。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: But I think that Nigeria is an interesting country. It's got a large population. It will be, actually, more populous than China at the end of the century. I mean, the forecasts are 750 million in Nigeria and 670-something in China on the latest UN forecast, I think.
transcript.zh: 但我认为尼日利亚是一个值得关注的国家。它人口规模庞大。事实上，到本世纪末它的人口将超过中国。根据联合国最新的预测，尼日利亚人口将达到7.5亿，而中国大约是6.7亿多。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: So, government has been, you know, government is very difficult to read in Nigeria because most of the time it seems hopeless. And then there are moments where it engages in bits of industrial policy that seem to work, as has happened with a number of sort of from basic products like fruit juice and chickens through to cement, which started off Aliko Dangote, the richest guy in Africa.
transcript.zh: 尼日利亚的政府运作非常难以捉摸，因为大多数时候它看起来令人绝望。但有时它推行的部分产业政策又似乎确实奏效，这体现在从果汁、肉鸡等基础农副产品，到水泥等一系列产业的崛起上，正是水泥成就了非洲首富 Aliko Dangote。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And then the protection that was afforded to him allowing him to build an oil refinery. And now he said he's going to build another oil refinery in Lamu in Kenya.
transcript.zh: 随后政府给予的政策保护，又让他得以投资兴建了一座炼油厂。如今他更表示打算在肯尼亚的拉穆再建一座炼油厂。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And he's also produces about half of the fertilizer required in Nigeria now, urea, and he signed to do a huge urea plant in Ethiopia as well. So there's a kind of an interesting, there are bits of government that sometimes get it right in Nigeria, and there's significant private sector capability.
transcript.zh: 他还供应了目前尼日利亚所需约一半的化肥——也就是尿素，而且他已签约准备在埃塞俄比亚建造一座大型尿素厂。所以情况很有趣，尼日利亚政府有时某些部门确实做对了事，而且其私营部门拥有相当强大的实力。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Well, with a city of 20 million people in Lagos, I mean, you'd think they'd at least not have the density problem.
transcript.zh: 像拉各斯这样拥有两千万人口的城市，你至少会觉得他们不会面临人口密度不足的困扰。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yeah. No, absolutely. And Lagos is now about a fifth of the Nigerian economy. It's the bit that works best. I mean, it's also kind of an advertisement for devolved power, because Lagos is a state as well as a city.
transcript.zh: 确实如此。拉各斯目前约占尼日利亚经济总量的五分之一，也是该国运转最好的部分。在某种程度上，它也是权力下放的一个正面范例，因为拉各斯既是一个城市，也是一个独立的州。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And a lot of what it does that seems to work, it does on its own, not as, not because it's asked to by federal government in Nigeria.
transcript.zh: 它所推行的很多行之有效的举措，大多是自主施政的结果，而不是受尼日利亚联邦政府的要求去做的。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Other countries, I mention Benin, small country in West Africa, I think is interesting. In North Africa, Morocco's having a lot of success at the moment bringing in foreign direct investment. It's got aircraft...
transcript.zh: 其他国家中，我提到的西非小国贝宁，我认为很有意思。而在北非，摩洛哥目前在吸引外商直接投资方面非常成功，他们发展起了航空……

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: ...of part manufacturers for Airbus and Boeing. But the biggest thing where it's getting traction is with car firms, and it started with French Peugeot and Renault, and now it's got the Chinese car companies coming in.
transcript.zh: ……比如空客和波音的零部件制造商。但目前势头最猛的领域是汽车企业，最早是从法国的标致和雷诺开始，而现在中国车企也纷纷涌入。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Because Morocco has a free trade deal with the EU, so it's seen as a...
transcript.zh: 因为摩洛哥与欧盟签有自由贸易协定，所以它被视为一个……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: A back door into Europe.
transcript.zh: 进入欧洲的后门。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: It's seen as a back door into Europe and the Chinese companies are going for that. And it's also seen as fairly safe in terms of US relations because you'll remember that Morocco recognized Israel as part of the Abraham Accords, and then the US has recognized its claim over, well, basically its colony of Western Sahara.
transcript.zh: 它被视作进入欧洲的后门，中国企业正是看中了这一点。而且从对美关系来看，那里也被认为相当安全，因为你应该记得，摩洛哥在《亚伯拉罕协议》框架下承认了以色列，随后美国也承认了摩洛哥对——嗯，基本上算是其殖民地的——西撒哈拉的主权主张。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Um, but anyway, people generally just see Morocco as a fairly safe place to go. Similarly, Egypt is a sort of US proxy. In the first 6 months of this year, there's just been a $10 billion integrated steel plant announced by Chinese investors.
transcript.zh: 总之，大家普遍把摩洛哥视为一个相当稳妥的去处。类似地，埃及某种程度上也是美国的代理人。今年前六个月，中国投资者刚刚宣布在此建设一座耗资100亿美元的综合钢铁厂。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And again, I think it's to do with lower-tariff access to markets than you can get from China now.
transcript.zh: 我同样认为，这是为了以比目前直接从中国出口更低的关税进入目标市场。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Fascinating. Let's widen out to sort of China across the continent. There is this very familiar, well-worn set of narratives about China in Africa: debt traps, land grabs, neo-colonialism, resource extraction that's dressed up as partnership.
transcript.zh: 太有意思了。我们把视野放宽到中国在整个非洲大陆的作为。关于中国在非洲，流传着一套人们耳熟能详、老生常谈的叙事：债务陷阱、掠夺土地、新殖民主义、披着伙伴关系外衣的资源掠夺。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Your book doesn't engage head-on with many of these, but it undercuts them, nevertheless, some of them anyway. I do want to ask you, having spent now years on the ground in Africa, are there popular narratives about China in Africa that your reporting contradicted, and are there ones that it more or less confirmed?
transcript.zh: 你的书并没有对很多这类说法进行正面交锋，但无论如何，至少在某种程度上动摇了其中一部分论调。我确实想问你，在非洲实地调研多年之后，你所做的调查是否推翻了某些关于中国在非的流行论调，又有哪一些是基本得到了证实的？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: No, I mean, you don't see a huge amount of media coverage that is hostile to China. Although, I would say that even under Trump II, in the polling that I've seen, Africans are quite favorable to China, but not as favorable as they are to the US. They're still more favorable to the US.
transcript.zh: 并没有，我是说，你其实看不到大量对中国持敌意的媒体报道。不过我想指出的是，即便在特朗普第二任期预期下，从我看到的民调来看，非洲人对中国固然相当有好感，但好感度仍不及对美国。他们依然更偏爱美国。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And in terms of what goes on, I think all kinds of things go on because my reading, really, is that Chinese firms and Chinese lenders respond to the environment that they find themselves in. If they find themselves working with a very corrupt government that expects to be paid off, and they want to do a project, and they can accept the cost of the payoff, they'll do the payoff.
transcript.zh: 至于具体发生的事情，我认为各种各样的情况都有。因为我的真实看法是，中国企业和金融机构完全是因地制宜，顺应当地环境。如果他们合作的是一个极度腐败、索要回扣的政府，而他们又想拿项目且能承受这笔开销，他们就会选择行贿。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And the Africans will extract that perhaps more easily than they would from an American or European company. But if they're dealing with a government that just wants to get the job done at the best possible price, then they'll do that.
transcript.zh: 非洲当地官员从中国企业那里敲竹杠，或许比从欧美公司那里容易得多。但如果他们打交道的是一个一心只想以最优性价比把项目办成的政府，他们也同样会按这种规矩把事情做好。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And the, you know, the overall consideration is that if you're talking about infrastructure, or really any kind of construction, you're getting a price from a Chinese contractor that you just could not get from from a European or US contractor because Chinese firms have cut the costs of these activities so much.
transcript.zh: 而且总的考量在于，如果是基础设施或者任何类型的建筑工程，中国承包商给出的报价，你在欧美承包商那里是绝对拿不到的，因为中国企业已经将这些项目的成本大幅压缩了。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: At the end of all of this reporting, of the whole writing process for this book, is there a core mental model that you've sort of arrived at for what China in Africa is? Is there a heuristic that you fall back on that captures what it is that Chinese actors in aggregate want in Africa?
transcript.zh: 在完成所有这些调研采访以及整本书的写作之后，对于“中国在非洲”到底是怎么一回事，你是否形成了某种核心心智模型？有没有一个能让你归纳出中国各类主体在非洲总体到底想要什么的认知法则？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: I think the main the main thing that I feel that Chinese investors indicate they want at the moment in Africa is better margins than they can get in China. Yeah, I mean, most businesses have horribly low margins in China now, right? Because there's no domestic growth, there's incredible levels of competition.
transcript.zh: 我认为目前中国投资者表现出在非洲最想得到的东西，就是比在国内更高的利润率。我是说，中国现在大部分行业的利润率都低得可怕，对吧？因为缺乏内需增长，竞争又极其激烈。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And so that tends to be what is getting getting manufacturers, in particular, interested in in Africa. They can produce often quite basic goods, but at much better margins than they'd get in China.
transcript.zh: 所以这往往就是吸引制造业者——尤其是制造商——前往非洲的原因。他们生产的通常是相当基础的产品，但利润率却远高于国内。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: That's an answer that would probably surprise a lot of people that that's what it comes down to and not some, you know, grand geostrategic plan. Where would you say the Chinese have been more and less successful, and why?
transcript.zh: 这个答案可能会让很多人大吃一惊：原来归根结底就是为了这个，而不是什么宏大的地缘战略图谋。在你看来，中国在哪些方面的参与比较成功，哪些不太成功？原因又是什么？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: I mean, on the plus side, you describe the infrastructure, the seven Beijing-sponsored industrial parks starting with, you know, Chambishi in the Zambian copper belt, the beginnings of this sort of manufacturing migration. There's thousands of Chinese factories accounting for something like 12% of African manufacturing value added.
transcript.zh: 我的意思是，积极的一面如你所描绘的基础设施建设，从赞比亚铜带省谦比希起步的七个北京支持的经贸合作区，以及这种制造业转移的开端。成千上万家中国工厂贡献了非洲制造业约12%的增加值。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: But on the other side, you have the Angolan kind of oil-for-loans deals whose terms are very kept secret and they've never been published. And they seem to leave this Angolan petrostate with less oil to sell at lower prices, and they get a $6 billion Chinese airport built in Luanda, but it took 20 years for some reason. So what distinguishes the Chinese engagement that has worked and the engagement that hasn't?
transcript.zh: 但另一方面，安哥拉那种“石油换贷款”协议的条款高度保密，从未公开过。这似乎让安哥拉这个石油国家陷入了能卖的石油更少、售价更低的境地；虽然中国在罗安达援建了一座耗资60亿美元的机场，但不知为何拖延了整整20年。那么，究竟是什么决定了中国在非参与的成与败？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: I mean, I'd say again that Chinese engagement that has worked in terms of things getting done on time and on budget is just who they're engaging with. And, you know, when they've done things in Ethiopia, the expectation is there that they're going to get done on time. Not everything gets done on time, but certainly the expectation is there.
transcript.zh: 我认为，中国项目能否按期、按预算顺利完成，关键还是取决于对接合作的对象。比如在埃塞俄比亚开展项目时，各方普遍预期项目能按时交付。虽然并非所有项目都能如期完工，但这种预期始终是存在的。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And I think where things have gone wrong for—well, where things went wrong for China's policy banks was when there was that tremendous...
transcript.zh: 我认为问题出在——或者说中国的政策性银行栽跟头的地方，在于当时出现了那种巨大的……

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: rush into Africa after 2013 because Belt and Road had had had the highest level of endorsement. And so the banks were seeking to lend to big projects.
transcript.zh: 在2013年之后涌入非洲，因为“一带一路”倡议获得了最高层的背书。因此，各大银行都争相为大型项目提供贷款。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And sometimes they picked their borrowers very badly, and as a result, they've had to reschedule and redefine loan terms for quite a lot of the lending.
transcript.zh: 有时他们挑选借款对象的眼光非常糟糕，结果导致他们不得不为相当大一部分贷款重新调整还款计划并重新界定贷款条款。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Right. So, you wrote this book against the backdrop of two American moves in 2025: the so-called reciprocal tariffs that briefly hit Lesotho and Madagascar. You know, countries whose only sin was exporting garments under America's own AGOA program, the African Growth and Opportunity Act.
transcript.zh: 对。你在写这本书时，恰逢美国在2025年出台的两项举措：其一是所谓的对等关税，一度重创了莱索托和马达加斯加。这两个国家唯一的“罪过”，不过是在美国自己的AGOA项目——也就是《非洲增长与机遇法案》框架下出口服装。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It hit them with some of the highest tariff rates in the world, and of course, also the gutting of USAID. In the same period, Beijing extended tariff-free access to all, I think it's like 33 of the least developed African states. It has tariff-free access to, now, I think, 52 states in Africa, is that correct?
transcript.zh: 这使它们面临着世界上最高的一些关税税率；当然，还有对美国国际开发署（USAID）的大幅削减。与此同时，北京方面向所有——我想大概是33个最不发达的非洲国家——提供了免关税待遇。它现在对非洲大约52个国家开放了零关税，是这样吗？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yeah, I think.
transcript.zh: 是的，我想是的。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You also describe the relationship between the World Bank and China in the '80s as something close to a model. The Chinese set the agenda, they asked for Eastern European economists who understood how to reform a communist system, and they became the Bank's biggest borrower. So is this another sort of model for how to interact with the World Bank?
transcript.zh: 你还在书中将20世纪80年代世界银行与中国之间的关系描述为近乎一种典范。中国人自己设定议程，要求指派理解如何改革共产主义体制的东欧经济学家，并且他们成为了世行最大的借款国。那么，这是否构成了与世行打交道的另一种模式？

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So, two questions kind of bundled together: What does the American retreat mean for China's position in Africa over the coming decades, with AGOA and the end of USAID? And does China, as a donor and more a lender than a donor and more a trade partner than either of the two, but does China practice anything like what it benefited from as a recipient in the '70s and '80s?
transcript.zh: 所以这里有两个连带的问题：随着AGOA的动摇以及USAID的收缩，美国的撤退对未来数十年中国在非洲的地位意味着什么？此外，中国作为一个援助国——虽然它更像是一个借贷方，而且比这两者都更是一个贸易伙伴——中国是否践行了它在七八十年代作为受援国时所获益的那套做法？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: I don't know. I suppose the point that I would make first is that, yeah, I mean, you're right. The US has retreated really from Africa. US trade with Africa is down about 40% on what it was 10 years ago, so it's, and that really reflects just extraordinarily little US interest in the continent.
transcript.zh: 这个嘛，我想我首先要指出的也是，没错，你说得对。美国确实从非洲撤退了。美国与非洲的贸易额相比十年前下降了约40%，这确实反映出美国对该大陆的兴趣极其匮乏。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: What has happened with AGOA has just been malicious, unpleasant, really driving already poor people to genuine poverty in terms of the effect that has in Lesotho or in Madagascar. The US, actually this week, has just said it's going to rescind AGOA membership for Rwanda from the start of next year.
transcript.zh: AGOA身上发生的事情简直是恶意且令人不快的，从其对莱索托或马达加斯加造成的影响来看，它真正把本就贫困的人群推向了赤贫。实际上就在本周，美国刚刚宣布将从明年初开始取消卢旺达的AGOA成员资格。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: And something like AGOA is just hopeless if you're going to
transcript.zh: 像AGOA这样的机制如果动辄……那根本毫无希望可言。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: You give it and take it away in an unpredictable way, because it's something that is supposed to encourage investors to respond to. And it did. In Ethiopia's case, AGOA got people like PVH, one of the biggest US garmenting businesses, to go into Ethiopia.
transcript.zh: 这种优惠给得飘忽不定、随意撤回，可它本该是用来激励投资者作出长期反应的。它确实一度奏效了：在埃塞俄比亚，正是凭借《非洲增长与机会法案》（AGOA），像PVH这种美国数一数二的服装巨头才进军埃塞俄比亚。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: But then during the civil war, the US government suspended AGOA for Ethiopia and everybody left. Left, yeah, so it was just awful. I mean, the Europeans are still there with the Everything But Arms arrangement. That's still there, but it is a real problem that the US behaves in this way.
transcript.zh: 但后来内战爆发，美国政府暂停了埃塞俄比亚的AGOA待遇，于是所有企业都撤走了。全部撤离，是的，这太糟糕了。欧洲人倒还在那里，保留着“除武器外全部免税”（Everything But Arms）的安排。这项安排依然有效，但美国这种做法确实是个大问题。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: In terms of China, you're right that China's given tariff-free access. But the problem with China is it doesn't buy anything. Or it buys very, very little.
transcript.zh: 至于中国，你说的没错，中国确实给予了免关税待遇。但中国的问题在于它什么都不买，或者说买得极少极少。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Just, yeah, commodities, raw materials.
transcript.zh: 就只买大宗商品和原材料。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yeah. Many, many people would say, "Well, that's the problem with China across the board," that it's running a, again, to use a very...
transcript.zh: 是的。很多人会说：“嗯，这也是中国面对所有国家时的通病”，它一直在搞……借用一个很……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: October is, a trillion already, is it trade surplus? On track to beat the 1.2 trillion for, 2025, yeah.
transcript.zh: 截至10月，贸易顺差就已经达到1万亿美元了？有望打破2025年创下的1.2万亿美元纪录，对吧。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yeah. So, I don't know whether China will sort of seek to double down on its position in Africa given that the US is pulling back, but certainly, as things stand, China's the only game in town, really.
transcript.zh: 是的。所以我不知道鉴于美国正在抽身，中国是否会选择在非洲加大投入、加倍下注，但毫无疑问，就现状而言，中国几乎成了那里唯一的选择。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: A last question for you, Joe, before we move on. A good part of this show's audience is in China, or works on China, and some of them make policy. The book ends by saying that in another decade, Africa's economy will be half again as big; that some multinationals are going to pile in too early, as they did in China maybe in the '80s and the '90s; that the wise are going to start small, they're going to hire locally, they're going to bide their time.
transcript.zh: 在我们进入下个环节之前，最后一个问题想请教你，Joe。我们节目的很大一部分听众生活在中国，或是从事中国相关工作，其中有些人甚至参与政策制定。你在书末提到，再过十年非洲经济规模将扩大一半；一些跨国公司可能会过早涌入，就像它们在八九十年代涌入中国那样；而明智的企业会从小处着手、本土化招募并等待时机。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: If a Chinese official or a Chinese company head were to read How Africa Works, what would you most want them to take from it? Is there something you'd want them to stop doing?
transcript.zh: 如果一位中国官员或中国企业高管读了《How Africa Works》，你最希望他们从中领会到什么？有什么事情是你希望他们别再做的吗？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: No, I mean, I think what I would want is for the Chinese government to look back at the input and the support it's had from the IMF, the World Bank, and different aid groups over the last 30 years and regard that as a benchmark for what China should be doing.
transcript.zh: 倒不是说别做什么，我认为我最希望的是中国政府能回顾一下过去30年里，它从国际货币基金组织（IMF）、世界银行以及各援助组织那里获得的投入与支持，并以此作为中国当前应该做些什么的标杆。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Certainly in Africa at the moment, when you talk to government people, you don't get the sense of China having any meaningful aid program. China does give grants, sometimes substantial grants, but they're on a sort of case-by-case basis.
transcript.zh: 当然，目前在非洲，当你与政府官员交谈时，你感觉不到中国有什么实质性的援助项目。中国确实提供无偿援助，有时数额相当可观，但往往是一事一议、按个案处理。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It does do stuff like capacity building, extension, things like that, doesn't it?
transcript.zh: 它确实也在做能力建设、技术推广这类事情，不是吗？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yeah, a little bit, but I think not much. I mean, what I'm told by government people in Africa is that the Koreans, for instance, seem to...
transcript.zh: 是的，有一点，但我认为并不多。我的意思是，非洲政府人士告诉我的是，例如韩国人似乎……

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: ...be much more active at the moment.
transcript.zh: ……目前要活跃得多。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Oh, interesting, interesting. All right. Well, thank you so much. Let's move on to this next section, which I call Paying It Forward. Is there somebody, Joe, who is doing work on African development or on China in Africa, that maybe more people should be paying attention to, should be reading? Are there maybe books or individuals? This calls for an individual nomination.
transcript.zh: 噢，很有意思，很有意思。好的。非常感谢你。接下来进入我们的下一个环节，我称之为“薪火相传”。Joe，有没有哪位学者或研究者在非洲发展或者中非关系领域深耕，值得更多人关注和阅读？有值得推荐的书籍或个人吗？这个环节主要是推荐具体的个人。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Well, there's a guy called Kurtis Lockhart at Africa Urban Lab, which is part of the African School of Economics.
transcript.zh: 嗯，有一位叫 Kurtis Lockhart 的学者，他在非州经济学院旗下的 Africa Urban Lab 工作。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Okay. What's he working on specifically?
transcript.zh: 好的。他具体在研究什么课题？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: He works on urbanization. So I'm now doing a bit of stuff with him at the moment, but he's been doing this for quite a long time.
transcript.zh: 他专注于城市化研究。我目前正和他开展一些合作，但他深耕这个领域已经有相当长的时间了。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Yeah, well, urbanization is one of your key pillars, so perfect. Sounds fantastic. All right.
transcript.zh: 是啊，城市化正好也是你理论的核心支柱之一，太合适了。听起来棒极了。好的。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: I just suddenly thought of Eric Pohlman at the One Acre Fund as well. The guys who support smallholder agriculture in Africa. And they've nearly got, they're going for like 10 million. They've got about 8 million people now.
transcript.zh: 我刚才突然又想到了 One Acre Fund 的 Eric Pohlman。他们专注于扶持非洲的小农农业。他们的受助规模快达到目标了，目标大概是一千万人，现在已经覆盖了大约八百万人。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Wow.
transcript.zh: 哇。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Pohlman is P-O-H-L-M-A-N.
transcript.zh: Pohlman 的拼写是 P-O-H-L-M-A-N。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Pohlman. Okay, got it. Thanks. So Kurtis Lockhart and then...
transcript.zh: Pohlman。好的，记下了。多谢。那就是 Kurtis Lockhart，然后……

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Eric Pohlman.
transcript.zh: Eric Pohlman。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: What about recommendations? Is there a book that you've read recently, or, you know, it can be anything—a movie, a travel destination, anything under the sun that you...
transcript.zh: 那好物推荐环节呢？你最近有没有读过什么好书，或者任何东西都行——一部电影、一个旅行目的地，天底下任何事物都可以……

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Well, I'm thinking of a novel that I love about sort of mad international travel. It's an old book, it was probably written in the '50s or '60s, called Earthly Powers by Anthony Burgess.
transcript.zh: 嗯，我想到了一本我很喜欢的小说，讲的是那种疯狂的国际旅行。那是一本老书，大概写于五六十年代，书名是 Anthony Burgess 写的《尘世权力》（Earthly Powers）。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Ah, Anthony Burgess, yeah. He's quite a writer. He wrote A Clockwork Orange, didn't he?
transcript.zh: 啊，Anthony Burgess，对。他是一位非常了不起的作家。他写了《发条橙》，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Exactly, he wrote A Clockwork Orange. But I think that, yeah, Earthly Powers is the book of his that I like very much.
transcript.zh: 没错，他写了《发条橙》。但我认为，《尘世权力》是他所有作品中我极为钟爱的一本。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Oh, I'll check it out. Excellent. Great recommendation. I'm going to recommend that documentary that I mentioned just now, Made in Ethiopia, by Xinyan Yu and Max Duncan.
transcript.zh: 噢，我一定找来看看。太棒了。很好的推荐。我打算推荐一下我刚才提到的那部纪录片，由余心妍（Xinyan Yu）和 Max Duncan 拍摄的《埃塞俄比亚制造》（Made in Ethiopia）。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
transcript.zh: 对，对，对。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: It follows the fortunes of a Chinese entrepreneur who runs an industrial park that I think you actually talk about it in your book. I mean, I feel like it sounded like you were describing the same industrial park, Dukem, outside of Addis.
transcript.zh: 它记录了一位经营工业园区的中国企业家的起伏经历，我觉得你在书里其实也提到了这个园区。我的意思是，感觉你描述的正是同一个工业园——位于亚的斯亚贝巴郊外的杜肯工业园（Dukem）。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: And, you know, all the problems as she's trying to expand to a second phase on some Oromo farmland, and you encounter sorts of trouble with cultural divides, of course, the arrival of COVID, and of course the Tigrayan War.
transcript.zh: 片中展现了她在奥罗莫人的农田上推进二期扩建时遭遇的种种难题，面对文化隔阂引发的各种纷争，紧接着又碰上了新冠疫情的爆发，当然还有后来的提格雷战争。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You should definitely check out Eric and Cobus over at the China Global South Podcast. They did an interview on their China in Africa podcast with the directors. It's really great. The documentary is just very, very well made. I think it won all sorts of awards. So yeah, that's my recommendation. I also highly recommend this...
transcript.zh: 大家一定要去听听 China Global South 播客的 Eric 和 Cobus 做的那期节目，他们在旗下的 China in Africa 播客中专访了两位导演。内容非常精彩。这部纪录片制作得极其精良，好像拿了各种奖项。所以，这就是我的推荐。另外我还强烈推荐这本……

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Visiting Mexico City. This is just a really lovely place. You know, even though I lived in Southern Arizona for a good part of my life, I have never actually come to Mexico City. This is my first time here, and very, very positively impressed.
transcript.zh: 参观墨西哥城。这里真的是个非常可爱的地方。尽管我生命中的很大一部分时间都住在亚利桑那州南部，但我以前还从未来过墨西哥城。这是我第一次来这里，留下了非常非常深刻且正面的印象。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: So, Joe, thank you so much for taking so much time to talk to me about your excellent, excellent book. Once again, it is called How Africa Works, and it's out, and I highly recommend it.
transcript.zh: 那么，Joe，非常感谢你花这么多时间和我就你这本极其出色的书进行交流。再次提一下，这本书叫《非洲如何运转》（How Africa Works），目前已经出版，我强烈推荐大家阅读。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Also check out Feyi's YouTube interview with Joe if you haven't gotten enough of it yet, from a more strictly, you know, without all the China angle in it. So thanks once again, Joe.
transcript.zh: 如果大家觉得意犹未尽，还可以去看 Feyi 在 YouTube 上对 Joe 的专访，那一期更多是从非洲本土视角出发，基本没有涉及中国角度。再次感谢你，Joe。

transcript.speaker: Joe Studwell
transcript.en: Well, thank you for having me on. I really appreciate it. I'm suffering a bit with a cold. I hope it wasn't too noticeable.
transcript.zh: 好的，谢谢你邀请我做客节目，我非常感激。我有点感冒受凉，希望在节目里听起来不算太明显。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: No worries, no worries. I'll get all of the nose-blowing out of it.
transcript.zh: 完全不用担心，没关系的。剪辑时我会把所有的擤鼻涕声都处理掉的。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: You've been listening to the Sinica Podcast. The show is produced, recorded, engineered, edited, and mastered by me, Kaiser Kuo.
transcript.zh: 您刚才收听的是 Sinica Podcast。本节目的制作、录音、工程、剪辑及母带处理均由我 Kaiser Kuo 亲自完成。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Support the show through Substack at sinicapodcast.com, where you will find a growing offering of terrific original China-related writing and audio. Email me at sinicapod@gmail.com if you've got ideas on how you can help out with the show.
transcript.zh: 您可以通过 Substack 平台访问 sinicapodcast.com 来支持我们，在那里您会看到越来越多精彩的中国议题原创文章和音频内容。如果您对如何协助办好节目有任何想法，欢迎发送邮件至 sinicapod@gmail.com 联系我。

transcript.speaker: Kaiser Kuo
transcript.en: Don't forget to leave a review on Apple Podcasts. Huge thanks to my guest, Joe Studwell. Thanks for listening, and we'll see you next week. Take care.
transcript.zh: 别忘了在 Apple Podcasts 上留下好评。非常感谢本期嘉宾 Joe Studwell。感谢您的收听，我们下周再见。保重。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 农业推广员 / 农技推广员
vocab_notes.note_zh: 指由政府派遣至农村基层，向小农推广良种、化肥施用技术和现代农耕技巧的专业技术指导员。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 自成一格的 / 独一无二的
vocab_notes.note_zh: 拉丁文法律与学术借词，用于探讨中国发展模式是完全无法复制的特例，还是东亚发展模式规模化后的产物。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 集聚经济 / 空间集聚效益
vocab_notes.note_zh: 城市经济学核心概念，指企业与人口在空间上高度集中时带来的规模效应、更精细的劳动分工及基础设施人均成本的大幅摊薄。
东亚政经经典范式，特指政府以推动国家经济现代化为核心合法性来源，并通过产业政策与金融操纵积极干预经济的体制形态。
政治学概念，指执政政权不依赖多党普选授权，而是通过持续提供经济增长、改善民生等实际执政业绩来获取民众认受性。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 拉手刹急转弯 / 政策方向的急剧掉头
vocab_notes.note_zh: 形象的英式俚语比喻，形容最高领导层在毫无预警或极其突然的情况下彻底逆转长期推行的经济或政治战略路线。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 石油国家 / 石油经济体
vocab_notes.note_zh: 指财政收入高度依赖原油出口、往往易陷入资源诅咒、制度脆弱且寻租盛行的资源型国家（如安哥拉）。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 互惠关税 / 对等关税
vocab_notes.note_zh: 国际贸易政策术语，在特朗普任内被用作反制外国贸易壁垒的惩罚性征税手段，曾波及享有关税优惠的非传统制造国。

references.title: How Africa Works: Success and Failure on the World's Last Developmental Frontier
